title.zh: 卷88 良吏:張恂 鹿生 張應 宋世景 路邕 閻慶胤 明亮
title.en: Volume 88: Virtuous Officials - Zhang Xun, Lu Sheng, Zhang Ying, Song Shijing, Lu Yong, Yan Qingyin, Ming Liang
title.raw: 卷88 良吏:張恂 鹿生 張應 宋世景 路邕 閻慶胤 明亮 Volume 88: Virtuous Officials - Zhang Xun, Lu Sheng, Zhang Ying, Song Shijing, Lu Yong, Yan Qingyin, Ming Liang

sentences.zh: 張恂 鹿生 張應[1] 宋世景 路邕 閻慶胤 明亮 杜纂 裴佗 竇瑗 羊敦 蘇淑

translations.literal: Zhang Xun, Lu Sheng, Zhang Ying, Song Shijing, Lu Yong, Yan Qingyin, Ming Liang, Du Zuan, Pei Tuo, Dou Yuan, Yang Dun, Su Shu
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun, Lu Sheng, Zhang Ying, Song Shijing, Lu Yong, Yan Qingyin, Ming Liang, Du Zuan, Pei Tuo, Dou Yuan, Yang Dun, and Su Shu

sentences.zh: 罷侯置守，歷年永久，統以方牧，仍世相循，所以寬猛為用，庇民調俗。

translations.literal: Having abolished enfeoffed lords and installed commandants, over many years the realm was governed through regional governors, generation after generation in unbroken succession; thus leniency and severity were deployed to shelter the people and harmonize custom.
translations.idiomatic: Once feudal lords were replaced by commandery administrators, power passed for generations through regional governors; governing meant balancing leniency and severity to protect the people and shape society.

sentences.zh: 但廉平常迹，聲問難高；

translations.literal: Yet unassuming integrity leaves but ordinary traces, and one's reputation is hard to elevate.
translations.idiomatic: Quiet integrity, however, leaves little to notice, and a sterling reputation is hard to win.

sentences.zh: 適時應務，招響必速。

translations.literal: Adapting to the times and meeting demands draws response swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: Those who seized the moment and met the needs of the age won fame overnight.

sentences.zh: 是故摶擊為侯，起不旋踵；

translations.literal: Thus those who seized and struck rose as marquises, ascending before they could turn around.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the bold could become marquises almost overnight;

sentences.zh: 儒弱貽咎，錄用無時。

translations.literal: The weak Confucian incurred blame and went unemployed for seasons.
translations.idiomatic: while the timid scholar was blamed and passed over for appointment after appointment.

sentences.zh: 此則已然於前世矣。

translations.literal: This had already come to pass in former ages.
translations.idiomatic: Such patterns were already plain in earlier times.

sentences.zh: 後之為吏，與世沉浮，季叔澆漓，姦巧多緒，所以蒲、密無為之化，難見其人。

translations.literal: Later administrators drifted with the age; as the younger generation grew thin and corrupt, cunning tricks multiplied in many strands—hence the unassuming governance of Pu and Mi was rarely to be seen in anyone.
translations.idiomatic: Later officials rode the currents of their day; morals grew thin and trickery proliferated, so the effortless, people-centered rule of Pu and Mi became all but impossible to find.

sentences.zh: 有魏初拓中州，兼并疆域，河南、關右，遺黎未純，擁節分符，多出豐沛。

translations.literal: When Wei first expanded into the central plains and annexed territory, in Henan and the lands west of the Pass the remnant populace was not yet settled; those bearing staffs and commission-seals mostly came from Feng and Pei.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Wei first opened the central provinces and swallowed new lands, the people of the Yellow River region and the western passes were still not fully assimilated, and most governors bearing imperial authority came from the old northern homeland around Feng and Pei.

sentences.zh: 政術治風，未能咸允，雖動貽大戮，而貪虐未悛，亦由網漏吞舟，時挂一目。

translations.literal: Their policies and manner of governance did not all succeed; though movement could incur severe punishment, greed and cruelty went unrepented—also because the net let great fish through, at times hanging but a single mesh.
translations.idiomatic: Their governance often fell short; though some who overstepped paid with their lives, greed and cruelty persisted, for the law's mesh was loose enough to let great wrongdoers slip through while only an occasional offender was caught.

sentences.zh: 高祖肅明綱紀，賞罰必行，肇革舊軌，時多奉法。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu made the statutes clear; rewards and punishments were invariably executed; at the outset he reformed the old tracks, and many at the time upheld the law.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen clarified discipline, enforced rewards and punishments without fail, and at first swept away old abuses, so that for a time many officials kept within the law.

sentences.zh: 世宗優遊而治，寬政遂往，太和之風，頗以陵替。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong governed at ease with a relaxed policy; the wind of the Taihe era declined considerably.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu ruled in leisurely fashion with ever looser policy, and the upright ethos of the Taihe reign faded markedly.

sentences.zh: 肅宗馭運，天下淆然，其於移風革俗之美，浮虎還珠之政，九州百郡，無所聞焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong held the reins, the realm was in turmoil; as for the beauty of transforming custom, or policies like floating tigers and returning pearls—among the nine provinces and hundred commanderies, none were heard of.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaoming the empire fell into disorder; nowhere among its provinces and commanderies could one hear of reforms that truly changed the people, or of the legendary probity symbolized by floating tigers and returned pearls.

sentences.zh: 且書其為時所稱者，以著良吏云爾。

translations.literal: Here we record those praised in their time, to set forth the virtuous administrators.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore record those acclaimed in their day as exemplars of virtuous officialdom.

sentences.zh: 張恂，字洪讓，上谷沮陽人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Xun, courtesy name Hongrang, was a native of Juyang in Shanggu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun, whose courtesy name was Hongrang, came from Juyang in Shanggu commandery.

sentences.zh: 隨兄袞歸國，參代王軍事。

translations.literal: He followed his elder brother Gun in returning to the state and joined the Prince of Dai's military staff.
translations.idiomatic: He followed his elder brother Gun home to Dai and served on the Prince of Dai's military staff.

sentences.zh: 恂言於太祖曰：「金運失御，劉石紛紜，慕容竊號山東，苻姚盜器秦隴，遂使三靈乏響，九域曠君。

translations.literal: Xun said to Emperor Taizu: "The Jin mandate has lost its grip; Liu and Shi contend in disorder; Murong has usurped the title east of the mountains; Fu and Yao have stolen the regalia in Qin and Long—so that the three spirits lack response and the nine domains are without a lord.
translations.idiomatic: Xun said to Emperor Taizu: "The Jin dynasty has lost control of the realm; the Liu and Shi families war in chaos; Murong has seized the throne east of the mountains, and Fu and Yao have stolen imperial authority in Qin and Long, until Heaven, Earth, and Man no longer answer and the empire has no ruler.

sentences.zh: 大王樹基玄朔，重明積聖，自北而南，化被燕趙。

translations.literal: Your Highness has planted your foundation in the dark north and renewed accumulated sage virtue; from north to south your transforming influence covers Yan and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness has laid your foundation in the far north and renewed the accumulated virtue of sages; your civilizing influence spreads from north to south across Yan and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 今中土遺民，望雲冀潤。

translations.literal: Now the remnant people of the central land gaze at your clouds and hope for your nourishing rain.
translations.idiomatic: The remnant people of the central plains now look to your clouds and long for your nourishing rain.

sentences.zh: 宜因斯會，以建大業。

translations.literal: You should seize this occasion to establish the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: You should seize this moment to found the great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 」太祖深器異，厚加禮焉。

translations.literal: " Emperor Taizu greatly valued his unusual talent and accorded him generous honor.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Taizu was deeply impressed by his talent and treated him with exceptional courtesy.

sentences.zh: 皇始初，拜中書侍郎，幃幄密謀，頗預參議。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Huangshi reign he was appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat; in secret counsel within the screen he often took part in deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Huangshi era he was appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat and often joined the inner councils of state.

sentences.zh: 從將軍奚牧略地晉川，拜鎮遠將軍，賜爵平臯子。

translations.literal: Following General Xi Mu in seizing territory in Jinzhou, he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance and enfeoffed as Baron of Pinggao.
translations.idiomatic: He followed General Xi Mu in campaigning in Jinzhou, was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Pinggao.

sentences.zh: 出為廣平太守。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Administrator of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 恂招集離散，勸課農桑，民歸之者千戶。

translations.literal: Xun gathered those scattered by disorder and urged farming and sericulture; more than a thousand households returned to him.
translations.idiomatic: Xun gathered refugees, urged farming and mulberry cultivation, and more than a thousand households came under his rule.

sentences.zh: 遷常山太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Administrator of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Administrator of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 恂開建學校，優顯儒士。

translations.literal: Xun established schools and gave preferential treatment to Confucian scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Xun founded schools and honored Confucian scholars.

sentences.zh: 吏民歌詠之。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners sang praises of him.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners sang his praises.

sentences.zh: 於時喪亂之後，罕能克厲，惟恂當官清白，仁恕臨下，百姓親愛之，其治為當時第一。

translations.literal: At a time when few could restrain themselves after the disorders of war, only Xun served in office with integrity, treating subordinates with benevolence and forbearance—the people loved him, and his governance ranked first in that age.
translations.idiomatic: In the aftermath of war, few officials could discipline themselves; only Xun served with spotless integrity and governed his subordinates with benevolence and forbearance. The people loved him, and his administration was ranked first in the land.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞而嘉歎。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu heard and commended him with sighs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu heard of this, he praised him warmly.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，賜帛三百匹，徵拜太中大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, he bestowed three hundred bolts of silk and summoned him as Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong came to the throne, he granted him three hundred bolts of silk and summoned him as Grand Master of Palace Counsel.

sentences.zh: 神瑞三年卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Shenrui, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of the Shenrui era, at the age of sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 恂性清儉，不營產業，身死之日，家無餘財。

translations.literal: Xun's nature was pure and frugal; he did not attend to estates, and on the day he died his household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was by nature pure and frugal; he did not build up property, and when he died his family had no wealth left.

sentences.zh: 太宗悼惜之，贈征虜將軍、并州刺史、平臯侯，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong mourned and regretted this, posthumously appointing him General Who Punishes the Barbarians, Inspector of Bing Province, and Marquis of Pinggao, with the posthumous title Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong mourned his loss and posthumously appointed him General Who Punishes the Barbarians, Inspector of Bing Province, and Marquis of Pinggao, with the posthumous title Xuan.

sentences.zh: 子純，字道尚，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Chun, courtesy name Daoshang, inherited the fief.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chun, courtesy name Daoshang, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 鎮遠將軍、平臯子。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the Distance, Baron of Pinggao.
translations.idiomatic: He held the rank of General Who Pacifies the Distance and Baron of Pinggao.

sentences.zh: 坐事爵除。

translations.literal: For an offense his enfeoffment was revoked.
translations.idiomatic: For an offense his noble title was stripped away.

sentences.zh: 純弟代，字定燕。

translations.literal: Chun's younger brother Dai, courtesy name Dingyan.
translations.idiomatic: Chun's younger brother Dai, whose courtesy name was Dingyan.

sentences.zh: 陳留、北平二郡太守。

translations.literal: Administrator of Chenliu and Beiping commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Administrator of Chenliu and Beiping commanderies.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈冠軍將軍、營州刺史，諡曰惠侯。

translations.literal: On death he was posthumously appointed General Who Conquers the Champions and Inspector of Ying Province, with the posthumous title Marquis Hui.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously made General Who Conquers the Champions and Inspector of Ying Province, with the posthumous title Marquis Hui.

sentences.zh: 代所歷著清稱，有父之遺風。

translations.literal: In his successive posts Dai won a reputation for purity, inheriting his father's legacy.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he held Dai earned a reputation for integrity, carrying on his father's ways.

sentences.zh: 代子長年，中書博士。

translations.literal: Dai's son Changnian, Erudite of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Dai's son Changnian served as Erudite of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 出為寧遠將軍、汝南太守。

translations.literal: He went out as General of Pacifying the Distance and Administrator of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General of Pacifying the Distance and Administrator of Runan.

sentences.zh: 有郡民劉崇之兄弟分析，家貧惟有一牛，爭之不決，訟於郡庭。

translations.literal: A man of the commandery, Liu Chongzhi, and his brothers were dividing their property; the family was poor and had only one ox, over which they could not agree and brought suit to the commandery court.
translations.idiomatic: Two brothers of the commandery, Liu Chongzhi and his kin, were dividing the family estate; they were so poor they owned only one ox, could not agree who should have it, and brought the dispute to the commandery court.

sentences.zh: 長年見之，悽然曰：「汝曹當以一牛，故致此競，脫有二牛，各應得一，豈有訟理。

translations.literal: Changnian saw them and said with distress: "You contend over a single ox and come to this; had you two oxen, each would have one—where would be room for litigation?
translations.idiomatic: Changnian saw them and said sadly: "You fight over one ox and come to court over it; if you had two oxen, each of you would take one—what reason would there be to sue?

sentences.zh: 」即以家牛一頭賜之。

translations.literal: " He thereupon bestowed one ox from his household on them.
translations.idiomatic: " He then gave them one ox from his own household.

sentences.zh: 於是郡境之中各相誡約，咸敦敬讓。

translations.literal: Thereupon throughout the commandery each warned the others and all practiced respect and yielding.
translations.idiomatic: After that, people throughout the commandery admonished one another and all cultivated respect and forbearance.

sentences.zh: 太和初，卒於家。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taihe era he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Taihe era he died at home.

sentences.zh: 子琛，字寶貴，少有孝行。

translations.literal: His son Chen, courtesy name Baogui, in youth showed filial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chen, courtesy name Baogui, was known from youth for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 歷武騎常侍、羽林監、太子翊軍校尉。

translations.literal: He served successively as Cavalry Constant Attendant, Supervisor of the Feathered Forest, and Colonel Adjutant of the Crown Prince's Protecting Army.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Cavalry Constant Attendant, Supervisor of the Feathered Forest, and Colonel Adjutant of the Crown Prince's Protecting Army.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子略，武定中，左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His son Lue, in the Wuding era, was Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lue, during the Wuding era, served as Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 鹿生，濟陰乘氏人。

translations.literal: Lu Sheng was a native of Chengshi in Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Sheng came from Chengshi in Jiyin commandery.

sentences.zh: 父壽興，沮渠牧犍庫部郎。

translations.literal: His father Shouxing was a Lang of the kugu department under Juqu Mujian.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shouxing had been a clerk in the treasury department under Juqu Mujian.

sentences.zh: 生再為濟南太守，有治稱。

translations.literal: Sheng twice served as Administrator of Jinan and was famed for his governance.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng twice served as Administrator of Jinan and won renown for his administration.

sentences.zh: 顯祖嘉其能，特徵赴季秋馬射，賜以驄馬，加以青服，彰其廉潔。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu admired his ability and specially summoned him for the autumn horse archery; he bestowed a piebald horse and blue robes to display his integrity and purity.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu admired his talent and specially summoned him to the autumn horse archery; he granted him a dappled horse and blue robes to honor his integrity and frugality.

sentences.zh: 前後在任十年。

translations.literal: In succession he held office for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: He held office for ten years in all.

sentences.zh: 時三齊始附，人懷苟且，蒲博終朝，頗廢農業。

translations.literal: When the three Qi regions had just submitted, people clung to shortcuts; dice games lasted all day and farming was widely neglected.
translations.idiomatic: When the three Qi regions had just submitted, people took easy ways; they gambled all day and neglected farming on a wide scale.

sentences.zh: 生立制斷之，聞者嗟善。

translations.literal: Sheng established regulations forbidding this; those who heard praised the goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng set rules forbidding this, and those who heard of it praised his good policy.

sentences.zh: 後歷徐州任城王澄、廣陵侯元衍征東、安南二府長史，帶淮陽太守、郯城鎮將。

translations.literal: Later he served successively as Chief Clerk of Prince Cheng of Xuzhou and of the Marquis of Guangling, in the eastern and southern campaign staffs, concurrently Administrator of Huaiyang and Commandant of Tangcheng garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as chief clerk on the eastern and southern campaign staffs of Prince Cheng of Xuzhou and the Marquis of Guangling, and concurrently as Administrator of Huaiyang and Commandant of Tangcheng.

sentences.zh: 年七十四，正始中卒。

translations.literal: Aged seventy-four, he died in the Zhengshi era.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the Zhengshi era at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 追贈龍驤將軍、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously appointed General of the Soaring Dragon and Inspector of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed General of the Soaring Dragon and Inspector of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 張應，不知何許人。

translations.literal: Zhang Ying — his place of origin is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ying — his native place is unknown.

sentences.zh: 延興中，為魯郡太守。

translations.literal: In the Yanxing era he was Administrator of Lu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yanxing era he served as Administrator of Lu commandery.

sentences.zh: 應履行貞素，聲績著聞。

translations.literal: Ying's conduct was chaste and plain, his reputation and achievements renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's conduct was chaste and plain, and his reputation and achievements were widely known.

sentences.zh: 妻子樵采以自供。

translations.literal: His wife and children gathered firewood to support themselves.
translations.idiomatic: His wife and children gathered firewood to provide for themselves.

sentences.zh: 高祖深嘉其能，遷京兆太守。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu greatly admired his ability and transferred him to Administrator of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu greatly admired his ability and transferred him to Administrator of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 所在清白，得吏民之忻心焉。

translations.literal: Wherever he served he was pure and upright, winning the heartfelt regard of officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he remained pure and upright, winning the wholehearted regard of officials and commoners.

sentences.zh: 宋世景，廣平人，河南尹翻之第三弟也。

translations.literal: Song Shijing was a man of Guangping, the third younger brother of Henan Intendant Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Song Shijing was a native of Guangping, the third younger brother of Henan Intendant Song Fan.

sentences.zh: 少自修立，事親以孝聞。

translations.literal: From youth he cultivated himself; in serving his parents he was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he cultivated himself, and in serving his parents he was known for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 與弟道璵下帷誦讀，博覽羣言，尤精經義。

translations.literal: With his younger brother Daoqu he studied behind curtains, reading widely among authors, especially expert in classical meaning.
translations.idiomatic: With his younger brother Daoqu he studied behind the curtain, reading widely among authors and especially mastering the meaning of the classics.

sentences.zh: 族兄弁甚重之。

translations.literal: His clansman Bian held him in high regard.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Song Bian held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，對策上第，拜國子助教，遷彭城王勰開府法曹行參軍。

translations.literal: Recommended as an Elevated Scholar, in the policy debate he ranked highest; appointed Assistant Instructor of the National University, transferred to Acting Aide in the Law Section of Prince Xie's opening staff.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as an Elevated Scholar, he ranked highest in the policy debate; he was appointed Assistant Instructor of the National University, then transferred as Acting Aide in the Law Section on Prince Xie of Pengcheng's staff.

sentences.zh: 勰愛其才學，雅相器敬。

translations.literal: Xie cherished his talent and learning and greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xie cherished his talent and learning and held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 高祖亦嘉之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu also commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu also praised him.

sentences.zh: 遷司徒法曹行參軍。

translations.literal: Transferred to Acting Aide in the Law Section of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Acting Aide in the Law Section of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 世景明刑理，著律令，裁決疑獄，剖判如流。

translations.literal: Shijing understood penal matters, worked on statutes and ordinances, resolved doubtful cases, and adjudicated like flowing water.
translations.idiomatic: Shijing understood penal law, drafted statutes and ordinances, resolved doubtful cases, and adjudicated with the ease of flowing water.

sentences.zh: 轉尚書祠部郎。

translations.literal: Transferred to Gentleman of the Secretariat Sacrificial Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Secretariat in the Sacrificial Section.

sentences.zh: 彭城王勰每稱之曰：「宋世景精識，尚書僕射才也。

translations.literal: Prince Xie of Pengcheng often said of him: "Song Shijing is penetrating in judgment—talent for Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xie of Pengcheng often said of him: "Song Shijing's insight is keen—he has the talent of a Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 」臺中疑事，右僕射高肇常以委之。

translations.literal: Doubful matters in the Secretariat, Vice Director Gao Zhao regularly entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: When doubtful matters arose in the Secretariat, Vice Director Gao Zhao regularly entrusted them to him.

sentences.zh: 世景既才長從政，加之夙勤不怠，兼領數曹，深著稱績。

translations.literal: Shijing was gifted in administration and from of old diligent and untiring, holding several bureaus concurrently with distinguished achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Shijing was gifted in administration and had long been diligent and tireless; holding several bureaus at once, he achieved distinguished results.

sentences.zh: 頻為左僕射源懷引為行臺郎。

translations.literal: Repeatedly the Vice Director Yuan Huai brought him in as Traveling Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Yuan Huai repeatedly took him on as Traveling Secretariat Attendant.

sentences.zh: 巡察州鎮十有餘所，黜陟賞罰莫不咸允。

translations.literal: He inspected more than ten provinces and garrisons; dismissals, promotions, rewards, and punishments were all fitting.
translations.idiomatic: He inspected more than ten provinces and garrisons; in dismissals, promotions, rewards, and punishments, none failed to be fitting.

sentences.zh: 遷徙七鎮，別置諸戍，明設亭候，以備北虜。

translations.literal: He relocated the seven garrisons, separately establishing various posts, clearly setting sentry posts to guard against the northern barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He relocated the seven garrisons, established separate posts, and clearly set sentry stations to guard against the northern barbarians.

sentences.zh: 懷大相委重。

translations.literal: Huai greatly relied on and valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Huai greatly relied on and valued him.

sentences.zh: 還而薦之於世宗曰：「宋世景文武才略，當今寡儔，清平忠直，亦少其比。

translations.literal: On returning he recommended him to Emperor Shizong, saying: "Song Shijing's civil and martial talent and strategy are rarely matched today; in clarity, impartiality, loyalty, and directness few compare with him.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he recommended him to Emperor Shizong, saying: "Song Shijing's civil and martial talent and strategy are rarely matched today; in clarity, impartiality, loyalty, and directness few can compare with him.

sentences.zh: 陛下若任之以機要，終不減李沖也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty employs him in crucial posts, he will in the end be no less than Li Chong.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty employs him in crucial posts, he will in the end prove no less than Li Chong.

sentences.zh: 」世宗曰：「朕亦聞之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong said: "I have heard of him too."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong said: "I have heard of him as well."

sentences.zh: 」尚書令、廣陽王嘉，右僕射高肇，吏部尚書、中山王英共薦世景為國子博士，尋薦為尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Prince Guangyang Jia, Vice Director Gao Zhao, and Minister of Personnel Prince Zhongshan Ying jointly recommended Shijing as Erudite of the National University, and soon after as Deputy Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Director Prince Guangyang Yuan Jia, Vice Director Gao Zhao, and Minister of Personnel Prince Zhongshan Yuan Ying jointly recommended Shijing as Erudite of the National University, and soon after as Deputy Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 王顯與宋弁有隙，毀之於世宗，故事寢不報。

translations.literal: Wang Xian bore a grudge against Song Bian and slandered him to Emperor Shizong; the matter lay dormant without response.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xian bore a grudge against Song Bian and slandered Shijing to Emperor Shizong; the recommendation lay dormant without response.

sentences.zh: 尋加伏波將軍，行滎陽太守。

translations.literal: Soon he was added General Who Subdues the Waves and Acting Administrator of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was given the additional title General Who Subdues the Waves and appointed Acting Administrator of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 鄭氏豪橫，號為難治。

translations.literal: The powerful Zheng clan was overbearing, known as difficult to govern.
translations.idiomatic: The powerful Zheng clan was overbearing; the region was known as difficult to govern.

sentences.zh: 濟州刺史鄭尚弟遠慶先為苑陵令，多所受納，百姓患之。

translations.literal: Inspector of Ji Province Zheng Shangdi's younger brother Yuanqing had earlier been Magistrate of Yuanling and accepted many bribes—the people suffered.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector of Ji Province Zheng Shangdi's younger brother Yuanqing had earlier been Magistrate of Yuanling and took many bribes, to the people's distress.

sentences.zh: 世景下車，召而謂之曰：「與卿親，宜假借。

translations.literal: When Shijing took office he summoned him and said: "We are kin; I ought to grant you latitude.
translations.idiomatic: When Shijing took office he summoned Yuanqing and said: "We are kin, and I ought to show you favor.

sentences.zh: 吾未至之前，一不相問，今日之後，終不相捨。

translations.literal: Before I arrived I asked nothing of you; from today forward we shall never part."
translations.idiomatic: Before I came I never questioned you; from today on we shall never be apart."

sentences.zh: 」而遠慶行意自若。

translations.literal: Yet Yuanqing acted as if at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yuanqing behaved as if unconcerned.

sentences.zh: 世景繩之以法，遠慶懼，棄官亡走。

translations.literal: Shijing restrained him by law; Yuanqing was afraid and abandoned his post and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Shijing restrained him by law; Yuanqing was afraid, abandoned his post, and fled.

sentences.zh: 於是僚屬畏威，莫不改肅。

translations.literal: Then the staff feared his authority and none failed to reform themselves in awe.
translations.idiomatic: Then the staff feared his authority, and all reformed themselves in awe.

sentences.zh: 終日坐於廳事，未嘗寢息。

translations.literal: All day he sat in the hall and never lay down to rest.
translations.idiomatic: All day he sat in the hall and never lay down to rest.

sentences.zh: 縣史、三正及諸細民，至即見之，無早晚之節。

translations.literal: County clerks, the three headmen, and common people of all ranks—he received them as soon as they came, with no distinction of early or late.
translations.idiomatic: County clerks, the three headmen, and commoners of every rank—he received them as soon as they came, with no distinction between early and late.

sentences.zh: 來者無不盡其情抱，皆假之恩顏，屏人密語。

translations.literal: Those who came none failed to pour out their whole hearts; he lent them a kindly face, dismissed attendants, and spoke in private.
translations.idiomatic: None who came failed to speak their whole mind; he would show them a kindly face, send attendants away, and talk with them in private.

sentences.zh: 民間之事，巨細必知，發姦摘伏，有若神明。

translations.literal: Matters among the people, great and small, he always knew; exposing wrongdoing and seizing the hidden, he was like a spirit.
translations.idiomatic: He knew every matter among the people, great or small; in exposing crime and catching the concealed, he seemed almost divine.

sentences.zh: 嘗有一吏，休滿還郡，食人鷄[單斤]；

translations.literal: Once there was an official whose leave ended and who returned to the commandery; he ate someone's chicken[1];
translations.idiomatic: Once an official whose term of leave had ended was returning to the commandery and had eaten someone's chicken;

sentences.zh: 又有一幹，受人一帽，又食二鷄。

translations.literal: There was also a clerk who accepted a man's hat and also ate two chickens.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a clerk who had accepted a man's hat and had eaten two chickens.

sentences.zh: 世景叱之曰，汝何敢食甲乙鷄[單斤]，取丙丁之帽！

translations.literal: Shijing rebuked them, saying: How dare you eat so-and-so's chickens[1] and take so-and-so's hat!
translations.idiomatic: Shijing rebuked them: "How dare you eat the chickens of one man and take the hat of another!"

sentences.zh: 吏幹叩頭伏罪。

translations.literal: The official and clerk knocked their heads and confessed guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The official and clerk kowtowed and confessed their guilt.

sentences.zh: 於是上下震悚，莫敢犯禁。

translations.literal: Thereupon above and below were shaken in awe, and none dared violate the prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: From that time on, high and low were shaken with fear, and no one dared break the law.

sentences.zh: 坐弟道璵事除名。

translations.literal: For his younger brother Daoqu's affair he was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his younger brother Daoqu's case he was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 世景友于之性，過絕於人，及道璵死，哭之哀切，酸感行路，形容毀悴，見者莫不歎愍。

translations.literal: Shijing's fraternal affection surpassed all others; when Daoqu died he wept with piercing grief that moved passersby, his appearance wasted and haggard—those who saw him none failed to sigh in pity.
translations.idiomatic: Shijing's brotherly love exceeded that of ordinary men; when Daoqu died he wept so bitterly that passersby were moved to tears, his face wasted and haggard, and all who saw him sighed in pity.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，母喪，遂不勝哀而卒。

translations.literal: After more than a year his mother died, and he could not bear the grief and died.
translations.idiomatic: A year later his mother died, and he could not bear the grief and passed away.

sentences.zh: 世景嘗撰晉書，竟未得就。

translations.literal: Shijing once drafted a History of Jin but in the end did not complete it.
translations.idiomatic: Shijing once undertook a History of Jin but never finished it.

sentences.zh: 子季儒，遺腹生。

translations.literal: His son Jiru was born posthumously.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jiru was born after his death.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，太守崔楷辟為功曹，起家太學博士、明威將軍。

translations.literal: At twenty, Administrator Cui Kai recruited him as Registrar; he began his career as Erudite of the Imperial University and General of Illustrious Might.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he was recruited by Administrator Cui Kai as Registrar and entered service as Erudite of the Imperial University and General of Illustrious Might.

sentences.zh: 曾至譙宋之間，為文弔嵇康，甚有理致。

translations.literal: He once traveled between Qiao and Song and wrote a funeral elegy for Ji Kang, very well reasoned.
translations.idiomatic: He once traveled between Qiao and Song and composed a funeral elegy for Ji Kang that was most finely argued.

sentences.zh: 後夜寢，室壞壓殞，年二十五，時人咸傷惜之。

translations.literal: Later one night as he slept, the room collapsed and crushed him to death; he was twenty-five, and people of the time all mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while he slept one night, the room collapsed and killed him. He was twenty-five, and all who knew of it grieved.

sentences.zh: 路邕，陽平清淵人。

translations.literal: Lu Yong was a native of Qingyuan in Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yong came from Qingyuan in Yangping commandery.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，積功勞，除齊州東魏郡太守，有惠政。

translations.literal: In the Shizong era, through accumulated merit he was appointed Administrator of Dongwei commandery in Qi Province, where he carried out benevolent administration.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Xuanwu's reign, through accumulated service he was appointed Administrator of Dongwei in Qi Province and governed with benevolent policy.

sentences.zh: 靈太后詔曰：「邕莅政清勤，善綏民俗。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling issued an edict: "Yong governs with purity and diligence and skillfully pacifies the customs of the people.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling issued an edict: "Yong has governed with purity and diligence and has skillfully soothed the people's customs.

sentences.zh: 比經年儉，郡內饑饉，羣庶嗷嗷，將就溝壑，而邕自出家粟，賑賜貧窘，民以獲濟。

translations.literal: In recent years there has been famine; within the commandery there was hunger; the multitude cried out and were about to fall into ditches and gullies, yet Yong brought out grain from his own household to relieve and bestow on the poor and distressed, and the people thereby found relief.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years there has been famine; hunger spread through the commandery and the people were on the verge of starvation, yet Yong brought grain from his own household to feed the poor, and the people were saved.

sentences.zh: 雖古之良守，何以尚茲。

translations.literal: Even the good administrators of antiquity could hardly surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: Even the finest administrators of antiquity could hardly surpass this.

sentences.zh: 宜見霑錫，以垂奬勸。

translations.literal: He should receive favor and reward, to serve as encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: He should receive favor and reward as an example to others.

sentences.zh: 可賜龍厩馬一匹、衣一襲、被褥一具。

translations.literal: Let there be granted one horse from the imperial stables, one suit of clothes, and one set of bedding.
translations.idiomatic: Grant him one horse from the imperial stables, one suit of clothes, and one set of bedding.

sentences.zh: 班宣州鎮，咸使聞知。

translations.literal: Proclaim this throughout the provinces and garrisons so that all may hear.
translations.idiomatic: Proclaim this throughout the provinces and garrisons so that all may hear of it.

sentences.zh: 」邕以善治民，稍遷至南青州刺史而卒。

translations.literal: " Because of his skill in governing the people, he was gradually promoted to Inspector of Southern Yan Province and then died.
translations.idiomatic: " For his skill in governing the people he was gradually promoted to Inspector of Southern Yan Province, where he later died.

sentences.zh: 閻慶胤，不知何許人。

translations.literal: Yan Qingyin — his place of origin is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Qingyin — his native place is unknown.

sentences.zh: [2]為東秦州敷城太守。

translations.literal: [2] He was Administrator of Fucheng in Eastern Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: [2] He served as Administrator of Fucheng in Eastern Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 在政五年，清勤厲俗。

translations.literal: In office five years, he was pure, diligent, and stern in reforming custom.
translations.idiomatic: In five years of office he was pure, diligent, and strict in reforming local custom.

sentences.zh: 頻年饑饉，慶胤歲常以家粟千石賑恤貧窮，民賴以濟。

translations.literal: In years of repeated famine, Qingyin every year used a thousand piculs of household grain to relieve and succor the poor, and the people relied on him for relief.
translations.idiomatic: In years of repeated famine Qingyin every year used a thousand piculs of his household grain to relieve the poor, on whom the people depended for survival.

sentences.zh: 其部民楊寶龍等一千餘人，申訟美政。

translations.literal: More than a thousand of his subjects, including Yang Baolong, petitioned praising his excellent administration.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand of his subjects, including Yang Baolong, submitted petitions praising his excellent governance.

sentences.zh: 有司奏曰：「案慶胤自莅此郡，惠政有聞，又能自以己粟贍恤饑饉，乃有子愛百姓之義。

translations.literal: The relevant office memorialized: "According to our investigation, since Qingyin took office in this commandery his benevolent administration has been heard of, and he was moreover able to use his own grain to feed and relieve famine—this is the righteousness of cherishing the people as children.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant office memorialized: "Our investigation shows that since Qingyin took this commandery his benevolent rule has been widely noted, and he was able to use his own grain to relieve famine—truly the conduct of one who loves the people as his children.

sentences.zh: 如不少加優賚，無以厲彼貪殘。

translations.literal: If he is not given some additional favor and reward, there is no means to admonish those who are greedy and cruel.
translations.idiomatic: If he is not given additional favor and reward, there will be no way to restrain the greedy and cruel.

sentences.zh: 又案齊州東魏郡太守路邕，在郡治能與之相埒，語其分贍又亦不殊，而聖旨優隆賜以衣馬，求情即理，謂合同賞。

translations.literal: We further find that Lu Yong, Administrator of Dongwei in Qi Province, in governing the commandery matched him in ability, and in sharing out provisions was likewise not inferior; yet the imperial edict specially honored Yong with gifts of clothes and horses. Judging by reason, we hold that equal reward is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: We further find that Lu Yong, Administrator of Dongwei in Qi Province, governed with comparable ability and was no less generous in sharing provisions, yet the imperial edict specially honored Yong with clothes and horses. By reason, we hold that equal reward is fitting.

sentences.zh: 」靈太后卒無褒賞焉。

translations.literal: " In the end Empress Dowager Ling gave no reward or commendation.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end Empress Dowager Ling granted no reward or commendation.

sentences.zh: 明亮，字文德，平原人。

translations.literal: Ming Liang, courtesy name Wende, was a native of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Liang, whose courtesy name was Wende, came from Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: [3]性方厚，有識幹。

translations.literal: [3] His nature was upright and generous, and he had insight and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: [3] He was upright and generous by nature, with insight and administrative ability.

sentences.zh: 自給事中歷員外常侍。

translations.literal: From Attendant within the Yellow Gates he rose through Supernumerary Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from Attendant within the Yellow Gates through Supernumerary Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 延昌中，世宗臨朝堂，親自黜陟，授亮勇武將軍。

translations.literal: In the Yanchang era Emperor Shizong held court in the main hall and personally promoted and demoted officials, appointing Liang General of Martial Valor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yanchang era Emperor Xuanwu held court in the main hall, personally promoted and demoted officials, and appointed Liang General of Martial Valor.

sentences.zh: 亮進曰：「臣本官常侍，是第三清。

translations.literal: Liang advanced and said: "My original office was Regular Attendant, which is the third rank of purity.
translations.idiomatic: Liang stepped forward and said: "My former office was Regular Attendant, which is of the third rank of purity.

sentences.zh: 今授臣勇武，其號至濁。

translations.literal: Now I am appointed General of Martial Valor, whose title is of the utmost impurity.
translations.idiomatic: Now I am given General of Martial Valor, whose title is among the most impure.

sentences.zh: 且文武又殊，請更改授。

translations.literal: Moreover civil and military are again different; I request a change of appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the civil and military ranks differ; I ask that another appointment be granted."

sentences.zh: 」世宗曰：「今依勞行賞，不論清濁，卿何得乃復以清濁為辭！

translations.literal: " Emperor Shizong said: "Now rewards follow merit and do not distinguish pure from impure—how can you again take pure and impure as your plea!
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Xuanwu said: "Rewards now follow merit and do not distinguish pure from impure—why do you again plead pure and impure!

sentences.zh: 」亮曰：「聖明在上，清濁故分。

translations.literal: " Liang said: "With sage clarity above, pure and impure are therefore distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: " Liang said: "With a sage emperor above, pure and impure are rightly distinguished.

sentences.zh: 臣既屬聖明，是以敢啟。

translations.literal: I now belong to that sage clarity, and therefore dare to speak.
translations.idiomatic: I now serve such a sage emperor, and therefore dare to speak."

sentences.zh: 」世宗曰：「九流之內，人咸君子，雖文武號殊，佐治一也。

translations.literal: " Emperor Shizong said: "Within the nine currents all are gentlemen; though civil and military titles differ, in assisting governance they are one.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Xuanwu said: "Within the nine currents all are gentlemen; though civil and military titles differ, in assisting governance they are one.

sentences.zh: 卿何得獨欲乖眾，妄相清濁。

translations.literal: How can you alone wish to defy the multitude and falsely distinguish pure and impure.
translations.idiomatic: How can you alone wish to defy the multitude and falsely distinguish pure from impure.

sentences.zh: 所請未可，但依前授。

translations.literal: Your request cannot be granted; follow the former appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Your request cannot be granted; accept the appointment as given.

sentences.zh: 」亮曰：「今江左未賓，書軌宜一。

translations.literal: " Liang said: "Now the lands south of the Yangtze have not yet submitted; writing and chariot-tracks ought to be unified.
translations.idiomatic: " Liang said: "The lands south of the Yangtze have not yet submitted; the empire's writing and roads ought to be unified.

sentences.zh: 方為陛下授命前驅，拓定吳會。

translations.literal: I am about to receive Your Majesty's commission as vanguard and open and settle Wu and Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: I am about to receive Your Majesty's commission as vanguard and open and settle Wu and Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 官爵陛下之所輕，賤命微臣之所重，陛下方收所重，何惜所輕。

translations.literal: Titles and offices are what Your Majesty holds light; this humble life is what your humble servant holds heavy. Your Majesty is just now taking what is heavy—why spare what is light?
translations.idiomatic: Titles are light in Your Majesty's eyes but heavy in mine; Your Majesty is now taking what I hold heavy—why spare what you hold light?

sentences.zh: 」世宗笑曰：「卿欲為朕拓定江表，揃平蕭衍，揃平拓定，非勇武莫可。

translations.literal: " Emperor Shizong smiled and said: "You wish to open and settle the lands south of the Yangtze for Us and level Xiao Yan—to level and open and settle, none but Martial Valor will do.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Xuanwu smiled and said: "You wish to open the south for me and level Xiao Yan—to level and settle, none but Martial Valor will do.

sentences.zh: 今之所授，是副卿言。

translations.literal: What is granted now answers your words.
translations.idiomatic: What is granted now suits your own words.

sentences.zh: 辭勇及武，自相矛盾。

translations.literal: To decline Martial Valor yet speak of martial affairs is self-contradictory.
translations.idiomatic: To decline Martial Valor yet speak of military service is self-contradictory.

sentences.zh: 」亮曰：「臣欲仰禀聖規，運籌而定，何假勇武，方乃成功。

translations.literal: " Liang said: "Your servant wishes to rely on and receive the sage rule, plan strategy and thereby settle affairs—why borrow Martial Valor? Only then will success be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: " Liang said: "I wish to rely on your sage rule, plan strategy and thereby succeed—why need Martial Valor at all?

sentences.zh: 」世宗曰：「謀勇二事，體本相須。

translations.literal: " Emperor Shizong said: "Strategy and valor are two matters whose substance fundamentally depends on each other.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Xuanwu said: "Strategy and valor are two things that fundamentally depend on each other.

sentences.zh: 若勇而無謀，則勇不獨舉；

translations.literal: If there is valor without strategy, then valor cannot act alone;
translations.idiomatic: Valor without strategy cannot stand alone;

sentences.zh: 若謀而無勇，則謀不孤行。

translations.literal: if there is strategy without valor, then strategy cannot go alone.
translations.idiomatic: strategy without valor cannot go alone.

sentences.zh: 必須兼兩，乃能制勝，何得云偏須運籌而不復假勇乎？

translations.literal: Both must be combined to overcome; how can you say you need only strategy and will not again borrow valor?
translations.idiomatic: Both must be joined to prevail—how can you say you need only strategy and need no valor?

sentences.zh: 」亮曰：「請改授平遠將軍。

translations.literal: " Liang said: "I request instead appointment as General Who Pacifies the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: " Liang said: "I ask instead to be appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance."

sentences.zh: 」世宗曰：「運籌用武，然後遠人始平，卿但用武平之，何患不得平遠也。

translations.literal: " Emperor Shizong said: "Use strategy and employ martial force—only then are distant peoples first pacified. You need only use martial force to pacify them; what worry is there that you cannot pacify the distance?
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Xuanwu said: "Use strategy and martial force together—only then are distant peoples pacified. Use martial force to pacify them; why worry that you cannot pacify the distance?"

sentences.zh: 」亮乃陳謝而退。

translations.literal: " Liang thereupon expressed thanks and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " Liang then expressed thanks and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 後除陽平太守，清白愛民，甚有惠政，聲績之美，顯著當時。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Administrator of Yangping, pure andupright loving the people, with very benevolent administration; the beauty of his reputation and achievements was conspicuous in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Administrator of Yangping, where he was pure andupright, loved the people, and carried out excellent benevolent policies; his reputation shone conspicuously in his day.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉其風化。

translations.literal: The court commended his transforming influence.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised his civilizing influence.

sentences.zh: 轉汲郡太守，為治如前，譽宣遠近。

translations.literal: Transferred to Administrator of Ji commandery, he governed as before, his fame proclaimed near and far.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Administrator of Ji commandery, he governed as before, and his fame spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 二郡民吏，迄今追思之。

translations.literal: Officials and people of both commanderies to this day recall him with longing.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and people of both commanderies still remember him with longing.

sentences.zh: 卒孝昌初，贈左將軍、南青州刺史。

translations.literal: He died at the beginning of the Xiaochang era; posthumously appointed Left General and Inspector of Southern Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the beginning of the Xiaochang era and was posthumously made Left General and Inspector of Southern Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 初，亮之在陽平，屬相州刺史、中山王熙起兵討元叉。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Liang was in Yangping, the Inspector of Xiang Province, Prince Zhongshan Xi, raised troops to attack Yuan Cha.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Liang was at Yangping, Prince Zhongshan Xi, Inspector of Xiang Province, raised troops to attack Yuan Cha.

sentences.zh: 時并州刺史城陽王徽亦遣使詣亮，密同熙謀。

translations.literal: At the time the Inspector of Bing Province, Prince Chengyang Hui, also sent an envoy to Liang, secretly joining Xi's plot.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Prince Chengyang Hui, Inspector of Bing Province, also sent an envoy to Liang to join Xi's plot in secret.

sentences.zh: 熙敗，亮詭其使辭，由是徽音獲免。

translations.literal: Xi was defeated; Liang falsified the envoy's testimony, and thereby Hui's reputation was spared.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi was defeated, Liang falsified the envoy's testimony, and thereby Hui escaped blame.

sentences.zh: [4]二年，詔追前效，重贈平東將軍、濟州刺史，拜其子希遠奉朝請。

translations.literal: [4] In the second year an edict recalled his former merit; he was again posthumously appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Ji Province, and his son Xiyuan was appointed Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: [4] In the second year an edict recalled his former service; he was again posthumously made General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Ji Province, and his son Xiyuan was appointed Attendant at Court.

sentences.zh: 亮從弟遠，儀同開府從事中郎。

translations.literal: Liang's younger cousin Yuan was Aide in the Opening Staff of the Parallel-Third-Rank Opening Office.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's younger cousin Yuan was Aide in the Opening Staff with Parallel Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 杜纂，字榮孫，常山九門人也。

translations.literal: Du Zuan, courtesy name Rongsun, was a native of Jiumen in Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zuan, whose courtesy name was Rongsun, came from Jiumen in Changshan commandery.

sentences.zh: 少以清苦自立。

translations.literal: From youth he established himself through purity and hardship.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he made his way through purity and hardship.

sentences.zh: 時縣令齊羅喪亡，無親屬收瘞，纂以私財殯葬。

translations.literal: At the time Magistrate Qi Luo died and had no kin to collect and bury him; Zuan buried him at private expense.
translations.idiomatic: When Magistrate Qi Luo died with no kin to bury him, Zuan buried him at his own expense.

sentences.zh: 由是郡縣標其門閭。

translations.literal: Thereby the commandery and county marked his gate and lane.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery and county thereupon marked his gate and lane in honor.

sentences.zh: 後居父喪盡禮。

translations.literal: Later in mourning for his father he fulfilled every rite.
translations.idiomatic: Later, in mourning for his father, he fulfilled every rite.

sentences.zh: 郡舉孝廉，補豫州司士。

translations.literal: The commandery recommended him as Filial and Incorrupt; he was appointed Clerk of the Ji Province Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery recommended him as Filial and Incorrupt, and he was appointed Clerk of the Ji Province Bureau.

sentences.zh: 稍除積弩將軍。

translations.literal: He was gradually appointed General of Accumulated Crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually appointed General of Accumulated Crossbows.

sentences.zh: 領眾詣淮，迎降民楊箱等。

translations.literal: Leading troops he went to the Huai and welcomed surrendering people such as Yang Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Leading troops he went to the Huai and welcomed surrendering people such as Yang Xiang.

sentences.zh: 修立楚鎮，超納山蠻李天保等五百戶。

translations.literal: He established Chu garrison and received more than five hundred households of the mountain Man Li Tianbao and others.
translations.idiomatic: He established Chu garrison and received more than five hundred households of the mountain tribes under Li Tianbao and others.

sentences.zh: 從征新野，除騎都尉。

translations.literal: Following the campaign at Xinye, he was appointed Commandant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Following the campaign at Xinye, he was appointed Commandant of Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 又從駕壽春，敕纂緣淮慰勞。

translations.literal: He again followed the imperial procession to Shouchun; he was ordered to go along the Huai to comfort and reassure.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed the emperor to Shouchun and was ordered to comfort the people along the Huai.

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史田益宗率戶歸國，[5]使纂詣廣陵安慰初附，賑給田廩。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yu Province Tian Yizong led households in returning to the state;[5] Zuan was sent to Guangling to comfort those newly attached and to relieve and supply field grain.
translations.idiomatic: When Inspector of Yu Province Tian Yizong led his households in submitting to the state,[5] Zuan was sent to Guangling to comfort the newly attached and distribute grain from the public fields.

sentences.zh: 從征新野，及南陽平，以功賜爵井陘男，賞帛五百匹。

translations.literal: Following the campaign at Xinye and the pacification of Nanyang, for merit he was enfeoffed as Baron of Jingxing and rewarded with five hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Following the campaigns at Xinye and the pacification of Nanyang, for merit he was enfeoffed Baron of Jingxing and rewarded with five hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 數日之中，散之知友。

translations.literal: Within a few days he distributed it among his friends.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few days he had distributed it all among his friends.

sentences.zh: 時人稱之。

translations.literal: People of the time praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 又詣赭陽、武陰二郡，[6]課種公田，隨供軍費。

translations.literal: He again went to Zheyang and Wuyin commanderies[6] to assess planting on public fields and supply military expenses as needed.
translations.idiomatic: He again went to Zheyang and Wuyin commanderies[6] to assess planting on public fields and supply military expenses as needed.

sentences.zh: 除南秦州武都太守。

translations.literal: Appointed Administrator of Wudu in Southern Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Administrator of Wudu in Southern Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 正始中，遷漢陽太守，並以清白為名。

translations.literal: In the Zhengshi era he was transferred to Administrator of Hanyang; in both posts he was famed for purity.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengshi era he was transferred to Administrator of Hanyang; in both posts he was famed for integrity.

sentences.zh: 又隨都督楊椿等詣南秦軍前，招慰逆氐。

translations.literal: He again followed the Commander-in-Chief Yang Chun and others to the Southern Qin front to summon and comfort rebellious Di.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Commander Yang Chun and others to the Southern Qin front to summon and comfort rebellious Di tribes.

sentences.zh: 還，除虎賁中郎將，領太倉令。

translations.literal: On returning he was appointed Commandant of the Tiger Guard and concurrently Director of the Imperial Granary.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he was appointed Commandant of the Tiger Guard and concurrently Director of the Imperial Granary.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂去職。

translations.literal: He left office on mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 久之，除伏波將軍，復為太倉令。

translations.literal: After a long while he was appointed General Who Subdues the Waves and again made Director of the Imperial Granary.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was appointed General Who Subdues the Waves and again made Director of the Imperial Granary.

sentences.zh: 尋除寧遠將軍、陰陵戍主。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed General of Pacifying the Distance and Commandant of Yinling garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed General of Pacifying the Distance and Commandant of Yinling garrison.

sentences.zh: 延昌中，京師儉，敕纂監京倉賑給民廩。

translations.literal: In the Yanchang era the capital was in famine; Zuan was ordered to supervise the capital granary in relieving and supplying the people's grain.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yanchang era the capital suffered famine; Zuan was ordered to supervise the capital granary in distributing grain to the people.

sentences.zh: 肅宗初，拜征虜將軍、清河內史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Suzong's reign he was appointed General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Interior Minister of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaoming's reign he was appointed General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Interior Minister of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 性儉約，尤愛貧老，至能問民疾苦，對之泣涕。

translations.literal: His nature was frugal and restrained; he especially loved the poor and elderly, even to the point of inquiring into the people's hardships and weeping before them.
translations.idiomatic: He was frugal by nature and especially cared for the poor and elderly, even weeping when he heard of the people's hardships.

sentences.zh: 勸督農桑，親自檢視，勤者賞以物帛，惰者加以罪譴。

translations.literal: He urged and supervised farming and sericulture, personally inspecting; the diligent he rewarded with goods and silk, the idle he punished with reproof.
translations.idiomatic: He urged farming and sericulture, inspecting in person; the diligent he rewarded with goods and silk, the idle he punished.

sentences.zh: 弔死問生，甚有恩紀。

translations.literal: In condoling the dead and inquiring after the living he showed great kindness and order.
translations.idiomatic: In condoling the dead and inquiring after the living he showed great kindness and care.

sentences.zh: 還，以本將軍除東益州刺史。

translations.literal: On returning, with his original general's title he was appointed Inspector of Eastern Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he was appointed Inspector of Eastern Yi Province with his former general's rank.

sentences.zh: 無御邊威略，羣氐反叛。

translations.literal: He had no strategy or prestige for governing the frontier; the Di tribes all rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: He lacked strategy and prestige for governing the frontier, and the Di tribes rebelled en masse.

sentences.zh: 以失民和徵還。

translations.literal: Because he had lost the people's goodwill, he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled for having lost the support of the people.

sentences.zh: 遷太府少卿，除平陽太守、後將軍、太中大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Grand Treasury and appointed Administrator of Pingyang, General of the Rear, and Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Grand Treasury and appointed Administrator of Pingyang, General of the Rear, and Grand Master of Palace Counsel.

sentences.zh: 正光末，清河人房通等三百人頌纂德政，乞重臨郡。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhenguang era, three hundred men of Qinghe including Fang Tong praised Zuan's virtuous governance and petitioned that he return to govern the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Zhenguang era, Fang Tong of Qinghe and some three hundred others commended Zuan's benevolent administration and begged that he be sent back to govern the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 詔許之。

translations.literal: An imperial decree granted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the request.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，為葛榮圍逼，纂以郡降榮。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era, besieged by Ge Rong, Zuan surrendered the prefecture to Rong.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiaochang era, when the prefecture was besieged by Ge Rong, Zuan surrendered it to him.

sentences.zh: 榮令纂入信都慰喻，都督李瑾欲斬，刺史元孚德纂，還。

translations.literal: Rong ordered Zuan to enter Xindu to offer reassurance and persuasion; the commander Li Jin wished to execute him, but the prefect Yuan Fu, who valued Zuan's virtue, had him return.
translations.idiomatic: Rong sent Zuan into Xindu to offer reassurance and counsel. The commander Li Jin wanted to have him killed, but Prefect Yuan Fu, who held Zuan in high regard, sent him back.

sentences.zh: 出，又勸榮以水灌城，榮遂以纂為常山太守。

translations.literal: After leaving, he again advised Rong to flood the city with water; Rong then made Zuan Administrator of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his return, he again urged Rong to flood the city with water, whereupon Rong appointed him Administrator of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 至郡未幾，榮滅。

translations.literal: Not long after he reached the prefecture, Rong was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely taken up his post when Ge Rong fell.

sentences.zh: 定州刺史薛曇尚以纂老舊，令護博陵、鉅鹿二郡，纂以疾辭。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Dingzhou, Xue Tanshang, because Zuan was old and experienced, ordered him to oversee Boling and Julu prefectures; Zuan declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Tanshang, Inspector of Dingzhou, considering Zuan's age and experience, assigned him to oversee Boling and Julu prefectures, but Zuan declined, citing illness.

sentences.zh: 少時卒於家。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home a short time later.

sentences.zh: 纂所歷任，好行小惠，蔬食弊衣，多涉誣矯，而輕財潔己，終無受納，為百姓所思，號為良守。

translations.literal: In the posts Zuan held, he liked to dispense small favors, ate plain food and wore worn clothes, and was often involved in deception and falsification; yet he was careless with money but strict with himself, never accepting bribes in the end, and was missed by the people, who called him a good administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his career, Zuan was fond of small acts of kindness and lived on simple fare in threadbare clothes, often resorting to deception; yet he was generous with money but strict with himself and never accepted bribes. The people remembered him fondly and hailed him as a good magistrate.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，贈平北將軍、殷州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era, he was posthumously given the titles General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Yinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongxi era, he was posthumously enfeoffed as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Yinzhou.

sentences.zh: 天平四年，重贈本將軍、定州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianping, he was again posthumously granted his former rank as general and the post of Inspector of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianping, he was again posthumously invested with his previous generalship and the post of Inspector of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 裴佗，字元化，河東聞喜人。

translations.literal: Pei Tuo, styled Yuanhua, was a native of Wenxi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Tuo, courtesy name Yuanhua, came from Wenxi in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 其先因晉亂避地涼州。

translations.literal: His forebears, because of the chaos of Jin, fled to Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors fled to Liangzhou during the turmoil of the Jin dynasty.

sentences.zh: 苻堅平河西，東歸桑梓，因居解縣焉。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian pacified Hexi, they returned east to their homeland and thus settled in Jie County.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Jian conquered Hexi, they returned east to their native place and settled in Jie County.

sentences.zh: 父景，惠州別駕。

translations.literal: His father Jing was Vice Prefect of Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Pei Jing served as Vice Prefect of Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 佗容貌魁偉，隤然有器望。

translations.literal: Tuo's appearance was imposing and grand, and he naturally possessed dignity and promise.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo was striking in appearance—tall and commanding—and bore an air of natural distinction.

sentences.zh: 少治春秋杜氏、毛詩、周易，並舉其宗致。

translations.literal: In youth he studied the Du commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals, the Mao version of the Book of Poetry, and the Book of Changes, and in each mastered its essential meaning.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he studied the Du commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals, the Mao recension of the Book of Poetry, and the Book of Changes, mastering the essential principles of each.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，以高第除中書博士，轉司徒參軍、司空記室、揚州任城王澄開府倉曹參軍。

translations.literal: Recommended as a xiucai, he was appointed a Doctor of the Palace Library with high rank, then became Aide to the Minister over the Masses, scribe-secretary to the Minister of Works, and Treasury Clerk of the Staff for Prince Cheng of Ren of Yangzhou's provisional office.
translations.idiomatic: Having passed the provincial examination with top honors, he was appointed Doctor of the Palace Library, then served successively as staff officer to the Minister over the Masses, secretary to the Minister of Works, and treasury clerk on the staff of Prince Cheng of Ren's Yangzhou headquarters.

sentences.zh: 入為尚書倉部郎中，行河東郡事。

translations.literal: He entered service as Director in the Granaries Section of the Ministry of Works and acted in the affairs of Hedong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Director in the Granaries Section of the Ministry of Works and dispatched to administer Hedong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 所在有稱績。

translations.literal: Wherever he served, he earned praise for his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served, his performance won acclaim.

sentences.zh: 還，拜尚書考功郎中、河東邑中正。

translations.literal: Upon his return, he was appointed Director of Merit Review in the Ministry of Works and Chief Clan Appraiser of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court, he was appointed Director of Merit Review in the Ministry of Works and Chief Clan Appraiser for Hedong.

sentences.zh: 世宗親臨朝堂，拜員外散騎常侍，中正如故。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu personally attended at the court hall and appointed him Extraordinary Attendant Cavalier-in-Attendance, retaining his post as chief appraiser.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu personally presided at court and appointed him Extraordinary Attendant Cavalier-in-Attendance while retaining his role as chief clan appraiser.

sentences.zh: 轉司州治中，以風聞為御史所彈，尋會赦免。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Administrative Aide of Sizhou; because of hearsay he was impeached by the censorate, but soon was pardoned by general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Administrative Aide of Sizhou but was impeached by the censorate on the basis of rumor; he was soon excused by a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 轉征虜將軍、中散大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Subdues Barbarians and Grand Master of Diffusion.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed General Who Subdues Barbarians and Grand Master of Diffusion.

sentences.zh: 為趙郡太守，為治有方，威惠甚著，猾吏姦民莫不改肅。

translations.literal: As Administrator of Zhao commandery, his governance had method; his authority and kindness were greatly manifest, and crafty officials and wicked people none failed to reform and obey.
translations.idiomatic: As Administrator of Zhao Commandery, he governed with skill; his firmness and kindness were widely felt, and corrupt officials and unscrupulous townspeople alike mended their ways.

sentences.zh: 所得俸祿，分恤貧窮。

translations.literal: The salary he received he divided to aid the poor.
translations.idiomatic: He divided his salary among the poor.

sentences.zh: 轉前將軍、東荊州刺史，郡民戀仰，傾境餞送，至今追思之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Front and Inspector of Eastern Jingzhou; the people of the commandery cherished and admired him, the whole territory turned out to see him off, and to this day they remember him fondly.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General of the Front and Inspector of Eastern Jingzhou. The people of the prefecture adored him; the whole region turned out to bid him farewell, and they still remember him to this day.

sentences.zh: 尋加平南將軍。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was additionally given the rank of General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon additionally appointed General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 蠻酋田盤石、田敬宗等部落萬餘家，恃眾阻險，不賓王命，前後牧守雖屢征討，未能降款。

translations.literal: Barbarian chieftains Tian Panshi, Tian Jingzong and others, more than ten thousand households in their tribes, relied on their numbers and blocked by terrain, did not submit to the royal command; successive governors though repeatedly campaigning against them, could not secure their surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal chieftains Tian Panshi and Tian Jingzong commanded more than ten thousand households. Trusting in their numbers and the rugged terrain, they refused to submit to imperial authority; successive governors had launched repeated campaigns against them without securing their surrender.

sentences.zh: 佗至州，單使宣慰，示以禍福。

translations.literal: When Tuo arrived at the province, he sent envoys alone to announce reassurance, showing them fortune and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuo took up his post, he sent envoys on their own to offer reassurance and show them the consequences of loyalty and rebellion.

sentences.zh: 敬宗等聞佗宿德，相率歸附。

translations.literal: Jingzong and others, hearing of Tuo's long-established virtue, one after another submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Upon hearing of Tuo's longstanding reputation for virtue, Jingzong and the others came forward in succession to submit.

sentences.zh: 於是闔境清晏，寇盜寢息，邊民懷之，襁負而至者千餘家。

translations.literal: Thereupon the whole territory was peaceful and quiet; bandits and robbers ceased; border people cherished him, and more than a thousand households came carrying infants on their backs.
translations.idiomatic: The whole province was soon at peace; brigandage died down, and more than a thousand border families arrived carrying their children on their backs, drawn by his reputation.

sentences.zh: 尋加撫軍將軍，又遷中軍將軍。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was additionally made General Who Pacifies the Army, and was again transferred to General of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon further promoted to General Who Pacifies the Army, then to General of the Central Army.

sentences.zh: 在州數載，以疾乞還。

translations.literal: After several years in the province, he requested to return on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: After several years in the province, he asked to retire, citing illness.

sentences.zh: 永安二年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 遺令不聽請贈，不受賻襚。

translations.literal: His final instructions forbade requesting posthumous enfeoffment and refused condolence gifts and burial robes.
translations.idiomatic: In his final testament he forbade his family from seeking posthumous honors and refused funeral gifts and burial vestments.

sentences.zh: 諸子皆遵行之。

translations.literal: All his sons followed this.
translations.idiomatic: His sons all obeyed these instructions.

sentences.zh: 佗性剛直，不好俗人交游，其投分者必當時名勝。

translations.literal: Tuo's nature was upright and blunt; he did not like to associate with vulgar people; those with whom he formed deep friendship were invariably celebrated figures of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo was forthright by nature and shunned the company of common worldlings; those with whom he formed close bonds were always the leading figures of the day.

sentences.zh: 清白任真，不事家產，宅不過三十步，又無田園。

translations.literal: Pure and honest, he followed truth; he did not pursue family property; his residence was no more than thirty paces, and he had no fields or gardens.
translations.idiomatic: Honest and unpretentious, he took no interest in building family wealth; his house measured no more than thirty paces across, and he owned neither farmland nor gardens.

sentences.zh: 暑不張蓋，寒不衣裘，其貞儉若此。

translations.literal: In summer he did not spread a canopy; in winter he did not wear furs—such was his integrity and frugality.
translations.idiomatic: In summer he went without a parasol; in winter he wore no furs—such was his austerity.

sentences.zh: 六子。

translations.literal: Six sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons.

sentences.zh: 讓之，字士禮。

translations.literal: Rangzhi, styled Shili.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rangzhi, courtesy name Shili.

sentences.zh: 武定末，中書侍郎。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuding, he was Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Wuding era, he served as Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 讓之弟諏之，字士正，早有才學。

translations.literal: Rangzhi's younger brother Suzhi, styled Shizheng, early had talent and learning.
translations.idiomatic: Rangzhi's younger brother Suzhi, courtesy name Shizheng, showed literary talent from an early age.

sentences.zh: 司徒記室參軍。

translations.literal: Staff Secretary to the Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Staff Secretary to the Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 天平末，入於關西。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianping, he went into Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tianping era, he went west to Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 竇瑗，字世珍，遼西遼陽人。

translations.literal: Dou Yuan, styled Shizhen, was a native of Liaoyang in Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yuan, courtesy name Shizhen, was from Liaoyang in Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: [7]自言本扶風平陵人，漢大將軍竇武之曾孫崇為遼西太守，子孫遂家焉。

translations.literal: [7] He himself said his origin was Pingling in Fufeng; the great Han general Dou Wu's great-grandson Chong became Administrator of Liaoxi, and his descendants thus made their home there.
translations.idiomatic: [7] He claimed descent from Pingling in Fufeng: Chong, great-grandson of the Han general Dou Wu, served as Administrator of Liaoxi, and his descendants settled there.

sentences.zh: 曾祖堪，慕容氏漁陽太守。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Kan was Administrator of Yuyang under the Murong.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Kan served as Administrator of Yuyang under the Murong clan.

sentences.zh: 祖表，馮文通成周太守，入國。

translations.literal: His grandfather Biao was Administrator of Chengzhou under Feng Wentong, and entered the state.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Biao was Administrator of Chengzhou under Feng Wentong before entering imperial service.

sentences.zh: 父冏，舉秀才，早卒。

translations.literal: His father Jiong was recommended as xiucai and died early.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jiong, a provincial graduate, died young.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，瑗啟以身階級為父請贈，詔贈征虜將軍、平州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Putai, Yuan petitioned using his own rank to request posthumous honors for his father; an edict posthumously granted General Who Subdues Barbarians and Inspector of Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Putai era, Yuan petitioned to have his father's rank raised posthumously, drawing on his own status; an edict granted his father the titles General Who Subdues Barbarians and Inspector of Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 瑗年十七，便荷帙從師。

translations.literal: Yuan at age seventeen already carried books and followed teachers.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen, Yuan was already carrying his books from teacher to teacher.

sentences.zh: 遊學十載，始為御史。

translations.literal: After ten years of traveling to study, he first became a censor.
translations.idiomatic: After ten years of traveling in pursuit of learning, he took his first post as a censor.

sentences.zh: 轉奉朝請、兼太常博士，拜大將軍、太原王尒朱榮官，因是為榮所知，遂表留瑗為北道大行臺左丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Court Gentleman for Attendance and concurrently Doctor of the Grand Chamberlain; he received appointment to the office of the Great General and Prince of Taiyuan Erzhu Rong, and because of this was known to Rong, who then memorialized to retain Yuan as Left Director of the Northern Route Great Office.
translations.idiomatic: He became Court Gentleman for Attendance and concurrent Doctor of the Grand Chamberlain, then entered the service of the Great General and Prince of Taiyuan, Erzhu Rong. Rong took note of him and had him retained as Left Director on the Northern Circuit Great Office staff.

sentences.zh: 以軍功賜爵陽洛男，除員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: For military merit he was granted the noble rank of Baron of Yangluo.
translations.idiomatic: For military merit he was ennobled as Baron of Yangluo.

sentences.zh: 瑗以拜榮官，賞新昌男。

translations.literal: Yuan, for accepting appointment under Rong, was rewarded with the rank of Baron of Xinchang.
translations.idiomatic: For entering Erzhu Rong's service, Yuan was rewarded with the title Baron of Xinchang.

sentences.zh: 因從榮東討葛榮，事平，封容城縣開國伯，食邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Then following Rong east to campaign against Ge Rong, when the matter was settled he was enfeoffed as Merit Marquis of Rongcheng county with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied Rong on the eastern campaign against Ge Rong and, once the rebellion was crushed, was enfeoffed as founding marquis of Rongcheng County with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 後除征虜將軍、通直散騎常侍，仍左丞。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed General Who Subdues Barbarians and Regular Attendant Cavalier-in-Attendance, still holding the left directorship.
translations.idiomatic: He was subsequently appointed General Who Subdues Barbarians and Regular Attendant Cavalier-in-Attendance while retaining his post as Left Director.

sentences.zh: 瑗乞以容城伯讓兄叔珍，詔聽以新昌男轉授之，叔珍由是位至太山太守。

translations.literal: Yuan petitioned to yield the Baron of Rongcheng to his elder brother Shuzhen; an edict permitted transferring the Baron of Xinchang to him instead, and Shuzhen thereby rose to Administrator of Taishan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan asked to transfer his Rongcheng marquisate to his elder brother Shuzhen; the court allowed him to pass on his Xinchang barony instead, and Shuzhen eventually rose to Administrator of Taishan.

sentences.zh: 尒朱世隆等立長廣王曄為主，南赴洛陽。

translations.literal: Erzhu Shilong and others established Prince Changguang Ye as ruler and went south toward Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Shilong and his allies placed Prince Changguang Ye on the throne and marched south toward Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 至東郭外，世隆等遣瑗奏廢之。

translations.literal: When they reached outside the Eastern Gate, Shilong and others sent Yuan to memorialize for his deposition.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching the suburbs east of the city, Shilong and the others sent Yuan to petition for Ye's removal.

sentences.zh: 瑗執鞭獨入禁內，奏曰：「天人之望，皆在廣陵，願行堯舜之事。

translations.literal: Yuan, holding his whip, entered alone into the forbidden precinct and memorialized, saying: "The hope of Heaven and the people alike lies with Guangling; we wish to perform the deed of Yao and Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan entered the inner precinct alone, whip in hand, and addressed the throne: "Heaven and the people alike look to Guangling. Let us do as Yao and Shun did.

sentences.zh: 」曄遂禪焉。

translations.literal: " Ye then abdicated to him.
translations.idiomatic: " Ye then abdicated to Guangling.

sentences.zh: 由是除征南將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Because of this he was appointed General Who Campaigns South and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was appointed General Who Campaigns South and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 敷奏侃然，前廢帝甚重之。

translations.literal: His memorials were forthright and composed; the Former Deposed Emperor greatly valued him.
