translations.idiomatic: His memorials were candid and assured, and the Former Deposed Emperor held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 出帝時，為廷尉卿。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xiaowu, he was Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu he served as Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 及釋奠開講，瑗與散騎常侍溫子昇、給事黃門侍郎魏季景、通直散騎常侍李業興，並為摘句。

translations.literal: At the ceremony of the sacrifice and the opening lecture, Yuan together with Regular Attendant Cavalier-in-Attendance Wen Zisheng, Gentlemen of the Yellow Gates Attendant Wei Jijing, and Regular Attendant Cavalier-in-Attendance Li Yexing all served as extractors of passages.
translations.idiomatic: At the sacrificial ceremony and inaugural lecture, Yuan joined Regular Attendant Cavalier-in-Attendance Wen Zisheng, Gentlemen-of-the-Palace Attendant Wei Jijing, and Regular Attendant Cavalier-in-Attendance Li Yexing in selecting passages for exposition.

sentences.zh: 天平中，除鎮東將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In Tianping, he was appointed General Who Guards the East and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianping era he was appointed General Who Guards the East and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 尋除廣宗太守，治有清白之稱。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed Administrator of Guangzong; his governance had a reputation for purity.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Administrator of Guangzong, where his administration won praise for its integrity.

sentences.zh: 廣宗民情凶戾，前後累政咸見告訟。

translations.literal: The temperament of the people of Guangzong was fierce and harsh; successive administrations all faced accusations and lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Guangzong were fierce and unruly; every previous magistrate had been dragged into lawsuits.

sentences.zh: 惟瑗一人，終始全潔。

translations.literal: Only Yuan alone, from beginning to end, remained wholly unstained.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan alone remained completely untainted from start to finish.

sentences.zh: 轉中山太守，加征東將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Administrator of Zhongshan, with additional appointment as General Who Campaigns East.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Administrator of Zhongshan and additionally appointed General Who Campaigns East.

sentences.zh: 聲譽甚美，為吏民所懷。

translations.literal: His reputation was very fine, and officials and people cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation was excellent, and both officials and commoners held him in affection.

sentences.zh: 及齊獻武王班書州郡，誡約牧守令長，稱瑗政績，以為勸厲焉。

translations.literal: When Prince Xianwu of Qi issued orders to the provinces and commanderies, admonishing and enjoining governors, prefects, and magistrates, he cited Yuan's administrative achievements as encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xianwu of Qi circulated edicts to the provinces instructing governors and magistrates, he held up Yuan's record as an example for others to follow.

sentences.zh: 後授使持節、本將軍、平州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was granted credentials with full authority, his former generalship, and the post of Inspector of Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later invested with full plenipotentiary authority as Inspector of Pingzhou, retaining his former generalship.

sentences.zh: 在州政如治郡。

translations.literal: In the province his governance was as when he administered a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He governed the province with the same care he had shown as a commandery administrator.

sentences.zh: 又為齊獻武王丞相府右長史。

translations.literal: He also served as Senior Clerk on the Right of Prince Xianwu of Qi's Chancellor's Office.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as Senior Clerk on the Right in the chancellery of Prince Xianwu of Qi.

sentences.zh: 瑗無軍府斷割之才，不甚稱職。

translations.literal: Yuan lacked talent for military office decision-making and was not very suitable for the post.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan lacked a talent for the decisive affairs of a military headquarters and was not well suited to the role.

sentences.zh: 又行晉州事。

translations.literal: He also acted in the affairs of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally charged with administering Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 既還京師，上表曰：

translations.literal: After returning to the capital, he submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Upon returning to the capital, he submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 臣在平州之日，蒙班麟趾新制，即依朝命宣示，所部士庶忻仰有若三章。

translations.literal: When your subject was in Pingzhou, I received the distribution of the new Linzhi regulations, and immediately according to court command proclaimed them; the gentry and commoners of my jurisdiction rejoiced and looked up as if to the Three Chapters.
translations.idiomatic: When I was in Pingzhou, I received the newly promulgated Linzhi code and immediately proclaimed it throughout my jurisdiction as the court had ordered. The people under my charge received it with joy, as though the Three Articles of Han had returned.

sentences.zh: 臣聞法象巍巍，乃大舜之事；

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that law's image towers high—it is the affair of Great Shun;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the majesty of law was the work of Great Shun;

sentences.zh: 政道郁郁，亦隆周之軌。

translations.literal: The governance path is flourishing—it is also the track of the flourishing Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: and that flourishing governance was the course of the ascendant Zhou.

sentences.zh: 故元首股肱，可否相濟。

translations.literal: Therefore ruler and ministers, approving and disapproving, assist each other.
translations.idiomatic: Ruler and ministers thus complement each other, each correcting and completing the other's judgment.

sentences.zh: 聲教之聞，於此為證。

translations.literal: The renown of civilizing instruction—here is proof of it.
translations.idiomatic: The spread of your transforming influence is proof enough.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下應圖臨宇，握紀承天，克構洪基，會昌寶歷，式張琴瑟，且調宮羽，去甚刪泰，革弊遷澆，俾高祖之德不墜於地。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty, responding to the chart and ascending the realm, grasping the calendar and receiving Heaven, is able to construct a great foundation and convene a glorious era, thereby extending zither and lute and tuning palace and note, removing excess and cutting luxury, reforming abuses and changing decadence, so that the virtue of the High Ancestor does not fall to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly reflect that Your Majesty, fulfilling the mandate and ruling the realm, holding fast to the cosmic order and receiving Heaven's charge, has laid a grand foundation and inaugurated a glorious age—harmonizing the realm as one tunes the strings of a zither, stripping away excess, reforming abuses, and reversing decadence, so that the virtue of the founding emperor may not be lost to the earth.

sentences.zh: 畫一既歌，萬國歡躍。

translations.literal: Once unification is sung, the myriad states leap with joy.
translations.idiomatic: Once uniformity of law is proclaimed, all the realms rejoice.

sentences.zh: 臣伏讀至三公曹第六十六條，母殺其父，子不得告，告者死。

translations.literal: Your subject, reading humbly, reached Article Sixty-six of the Three Dukes Section: "If the mother kills his father, the son may not report it; one who reports is put to death."
translations.idiomatic: In reading through the code, I came to Article Sixty-six of the Three Ducal Offices Bureau: "If a mother kills the father, the son may not report it; whoever reports it shall die."

sentences.zh: 再三返覆之，未得其門。

translations.literal: Repeatedly turning it over, I have not found the key.
translations.idiomatic: I have turned it over again and again but cannot see my way into it.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 案律，子孫告父母、祖父母者死。

translations.literal: According to the statutes, descendants who report parents or grandparents are put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Under the statutes, any descendant who accuses a parent or grandparent is subject to death.

sentences.zh: 又漢宣云：子匿父母，孫匿大父母，皆勿論。

translations.literal: Moreover Han Xuandi said: "A son who conceals his parents, a grandson who conceals his grandparents—all are not prosecuted."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Emperor Xuandi of Han declared: "A son who conceals his parents, or a grandson who conceals his grandparents, shall not be punished."

sentences.zh: 蓋謂父母、祖父母，小者攘羊，甚者殺害之類，恩須相隱，律抑不言。

translations.literal: This means that regarding parents and grandparents, from minor matters such as stealing sheep to serious ones such as killing—the favor owed requires mutual concealment; the law suppresses speech.
translations.idiomatic: The intent was that toward parents and grandparents—even for petty offenses like stealing a sheep, or grave ones like homicide—familial duty requires mutual concealment, and the law forbids disclosure.

sentences.zh: 法理如是，足見其直。

translations.literal: The principle of law is thus; it is sufficient to see its straightforwardness.
translations.idiomatic: The logic of the law is clear enough, and its justice is plain.

sentences.zh: 未必指母殺父止子不言也。

translations.literal: It does not necessarily mean that when the mother kills the father, the son alone must not speak.
translations.idiomatic: This need not be read to mean that when a mother kills the father, the son alone is forbidden to speak.

sentences.zh: 若父殺母，乃是夫殺妻，母卑於父，此子不告是也。

translations.literal: If the father kills the mother, this is the husband killing the wife; the mother is inferior to the father—here the son not reporting is appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: If the father kills the mother, that is a husband killing his wife; as the mother ranks below the father, it is fitting that the son not accuse him.

sentences.zh: 而母殺父，不聽子告，臣誠下愚，輒以為惑。

translations.literal: But when the mother kills the father, not permitting the son to report—your subject is truly low and foolish, but I venture to find this puzzling.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when the mother kills the father, the son is forbidden to report it—I am but a dull petitioner, yet I cannot help finding this perplexing.

sentences.zh: 昔楚康王欲殺令尹子南，其子棄疾為王御士而上告焉。

translations.literal: Formerly King Kang of Chu wished to kill Grand Tutor Zinan; his son Qiji, who served the king as charioteer-attendant, reported this to him.
translations.idiomatic: In olden times King Kang of Chu planned to kill the chief minister Zinan; Zinan's son Qiji, who served as the king's charioteer, reported the plot to his father.

sentences.zh: [8]對曰：「泄命重刑，臣不為也。

translations.literal: [8] He replied: "To leak a command is a grave offense; your subject will not do it.
translations.idiomatic: [8] He answered, "Disclosing such a command is a capital crime—I will not do it.

sentences.zh: 」王遂殺子南。

translations.literal: " The king then killed Zinan.
translations.idiomatic: The king then executed Zinan.

sentences.zh: 其徒曰：「行乎？

translations.literal: His attendants said: "Shall we leave?
translations.idiomatic: His attendants said, "Shall we flee?

sentences.zh: 」「吾與殺吾父，行將焉入！

translations.literal: " "I helped kill my own father—where would I go if I fled!
translations.idiomatic: "I helped kill my own father—where could I go if I fled!

sentences.zh: 」曰：「臣乎？

translations.literal: " They said: "Will you serve him?
translations.idiomatic: They asked, "Will you still serve as his minister?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「殺父事讎，吾不忍。

translations.literal: " He said: "To serve the killer of my father as my lord—I cannot bear it.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "To serve as minister to the man who killed my father—I cannot endure it.

sentences.zh: 」乃縊而死。

translations.literal: " Then he hanged himself and died.
translations.idiomatic: Then he hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 注云：棄疾自謂不告父為與殺，謂王為讎，皆非禮，春秋譏焉。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Qiji held that not informing his father was complicity in the killing, and that treating the king as an enemy was also against ritual—the Spring and Autumn Annals censured this.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator states that Qiji regarded failure to warn his father as complicity in the killing and treating the king as an enemy as also unritual—the Spring and Autumn Annals rebuked him for this.

sentences.zh: 斯蓋門外之治，以義斷恩，知君殺父而子不告，是也。

translations.literal: That case concerned governance outside the household, where righteousness severs affection—knowing the ruler would kill one's father and the son not informing him was correct.
translations.idiomatic: That case belonged to the sphere outside the home, where duty overrides private bonds—knowing the ruler would kill one's father and the son not informing him was right.

sentences.zh: 母之於父，同在門內，恩無可掩，義無斷割。

translations.literal: A mother toward a father—they are both within the household; affection cannot be concealed, and righteousness cannot be severed.
translations.idiomatic: Mother and father both belong within the household; natural affection cannot be hidden, and moral obligation cannot be cut away.

sentences.zh: 知母將殺，理應告父；

translations.literal: If one knows the mother is about to kill him, one should rationally inform the father;
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the mother intends to kill him, one ought to warn the father;

sentences.zh: 如其已殺，宜聽告官。

translations.literal: if she has already killed him, one should allow reporting to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: if she has already done so, one should permit reporting it to officials.

sentences.zh: 今母殺父而子不告，便是知母而不知父。

translations.literal: Now, if the mother kills the father and the son does not report it, this is knowing the mother but not knowing the father.
translations.idiomatic: For the mother to kill the father while the son stays silent is to acknowledge the mother but not the father.

sentences.zh: 識比野人，義近禽獸。

translations.literal: Understanding comparable to a rustic; righteousness nearing that of beasts.
translations.idiomatic: Such understanding is on a par with a barbarian's, and such righteousness barely above that of beasts.

sentences.zh: 且母之於父，作合移天，既殺己之天，復殺子之天，二天頓毀，豈容頓默！

translations.literal: Moreover, the mother toward the father joined in marriage and transferred heaven; having killed her own heaven and again killing the son's heaven—two heavens suddenly destroyed—how can sudden silence be tolerated!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in marrying the father the mother became his partner in a bond likened to heaven; she has destroyed her own heaven and her child's heaven as well—two heavens overturned at once—how could one remain utterly silent!

sentences.zh: 此母之罪，義在不赦。

translations.literal: This mother's crime, in righteousness, is unpardonable.
translations.idiomatic: The mother's crime, by right, should not be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 下手之日，母恩即離，仍以母道不告，鄙臣所以致惑。

translations.literal: On the day the deed was done, maternal affection departed; still to withhold report out of filial duty toward the mother is why this lowly minister is perplexed.
translations.idiomatic: From the day she struck, the bond of motherly affection was severed; yet to refrain from reporting out of filial duty toward the mother—that is what puzzles this humble official.

sentences.zh: 今聖化淳洽，穆如韶夏，食椹懷音，梟鏡猶變，況承風禀教，識善知惡之民哉。

translations.literal: Now sagely transformation is pure and harmonious, solemn as Shao and Xia; those who ate mulberries cherished music, owls and mirror-image birds still changed—how much more the people who receive the wind and embody instruction, who know good and evil!
translations.idiomatic: Today's enlightened rule is pure and harmonious, majestic as the music of Shao and Xia; even those who ate mulberries came to cherish music, and even fierce owls were transformed by the mirror—how much more the people who live under your instruction and can tell good from evil!

sentences.zh: 脫下愚不移，事在言外，如或有之，可臨時議罪，何用豫制斯條，用為訓誡。

translations.literal: If the lowly and stubborn do not change, that lies beyond words; if any such cases arise, guilt can be deliberated at the time—why pre-establish this clause as instruction and admonition?
translations.idiomatic: If some remain stubbornly unimproved, that is another matter; should such cases occur, punishment can be determined when they arise—what need to prescribe this rule in advance as a general lesson?

sentences.zh: 誠恐千載之下，談者諠譁，以明明大朝，有尊母卑父之論。

translations.literal: Truly fearing that a thousand years hence, talkers will clamor, thinking this illustrious great dynasty had a doctrine of honoring the mother and demeaning the father.
translations.idiomatic: I truly fear that in ages to come people will cry out in alarm, saying this glorious dynasty upheld a doctrine that honored the mother above the father.

sentences.zh: 以臣管見，實所不取。

translations.literal: In this minister's narrow view, it is truly not acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble opinion, that is unacceptable.

sentences.zh: 如在淳風厚俗，必欲行之。

translations.literal: If in pure customs and thick morals one must still enact it,
translations.idiomatic: If, amid pure customs and solid mores, you still insist on implementing it—

sentences.zh: 且君、父一也。

translations.literal: moreover, ruler and father are one.
translations.idiomatic: moreover, the ruler and the father are one in principle.

sentences.zh: 父者子之天，被殺事重，宜附「父謀反大逆子得告」之條。

translations.literal: The father is the son's heaven; being killed is a grave matter—it should be attached to the provision "if the father plots rebellion or great treason, the son may report him."
translations.idiomatic: The father is the son's heaven; his murder is a grave matter and should be covered by the statute allowing a son to report a father who plots rebellion or treason.

sentences.zh: 父一而已，至情可見。

translations.literal: The father is only one; the utmost affection is evident.
translations.idiomatic: There is only one father—the depth of filial feeling speaks for itself.

sentences.zh: 竊惟聖主有作，明賢贊成，光國寧民，厥用為大，非下走頑蔽所能上測。

translations.literal: I privately consider that the sage ruler initiates, bright worthies assist, illuminating the state and calming the people—its use is great; not something this low runner's dull obscurity can fathom from below.
translations.idiomatic: I know well that the sage sovereign acts with worthy ministers to support him, bringing glory to the state and peace to the people—matters far too great for a dull subordinate like me to presume to judge from below.

sentences.zh: 但受恩深重，輒獻瞽言，儻蒙收察，乞付評議。

translations.literal: But having received deep favor, I presume to offer blind words; if graciously received for examination, I beg it be referred for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet having received such deep kindness from you, I venture these ignorant remarks; if you will deign to consider them, I ask that they be submitted for collective review.

sentences.zh: 詔付尚書，三公郎封君義立判云：「身體髮膚，受之父母，生我勞悴，續莫大焉。

translations.literal: An edict referred it to the Ministry of State Affairs; the Three Excellencies' bureau director Feng Junyi rendered judgment saying: "Body, hair, and skin, received from parents; bearing and rearing me with toil—the continuation is nothing greater.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the case sent to the Ministry of State Affairs; Feng Junyi of the Three Excellencies' bureau delivered a ruling: "Our bodies, hair, and skin we receive from our parents; their bearing and raising us in weariness is the greatest of continuities.

sentences.zh: 子於父母，同氣異息，終天靡報，在情一也。

translations.literal: The child toward parents—same breath, different exhalations; a lifetime without repayment—in feeling, one.
translations.idiomatic: Toward both parents the child shares one vital breath, yet owes a debt that can never be repaid in a lifetime—in emotion they are one.

sentences.zh: 今忽欲論其尊卑，辨其優劣，推心未忍，訪古無據。

translations.literal: Now suddenly to discuss their honor and lowliness, distinguish superiority and inferiority—in heart one cannot bear it; inquiry of antiquity has no basis.
translations.idiomatic: Now suddenly to debate their rank and weigh one against the other—my heart cannot bear it, and antiquity offers no warrant.

sentences.zh: 母殺其父，子復告母，母由告死，便是子殺。

translations.literal: The mother kills his father; the child again reports the mother—the mother dies through report, and this is the child killing.
translations.idiomatic: If the mother kills his father and the child then reports the mother, and the mother dies because of that report, the child has effectively killed her.

sentences.zh: 天下未有無母之國，不知此子將欲何之！

translations.literal: Under heaven there has never been a state without mothers—who knows where this child would go!
translations.idiomatic: There is no land under heaven without mothers—where would such a child turn!

sentences.zh: 案春秋，莊公元年，不稱即位，文姜出故。

translations.literal: Examining the Spring and Autumn Annals: in the first year of Duke Zhuang, he is not styled as ascending the throne—because Wen Jiang was driven out.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals record that in Duke Zhuang's first year he is not said to have taken the throne, because Wen Jiang had been expelled for her crime.

sentences.zh: 服虔注云：『文姜通兄齊襄，與殺公而不反。

translations.literal: Fu Qian's commentary says: 'Wen Jiang had relations with her elder brother Duke Xiang of Qi, participated in killing the Duke and did not return.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Qian commented: 'Wen Jiang had an illicit affair with her brother Duke Xiang of Qi, took part in killing Duke Huan, and did not return home.

sentences.zh: 父殺母出，隱痛深諱。

translations.literal: The father was killed, the mother expelled—hidden grief, deeply concealed.
translations.idiomatic: Her father had been killed and her mother banished; in concealed grief he deeply hid the matter.

sentences.zh: 期而中練，思慕少殺，念至於母。

translations.literal: At the end of the first mourning period and into the second, yearning slightly diminished, thoughts reached the mother.
translations.idiomatic: At the midpoint of the second year of mourning, as his grief slightly eased, his thoughts turned to his mother.

sentences.zh: 故經書：三月夫人遜於齊。

translations.literal: Therefore the classic records: In the third month the lady withdrew to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the chronicle states: In the third month the lady departed for Qi.

sentences.zh: 』既有念母深諱之文，明無讎疾告列之理。

translations.literal: ' Since there is text of cherishing the mother and deeply concealing, clearly there is no principle of enmity and reporting publicly.
translations.idiomatic: Where the text shows him yearning for his mother while keeping the matter hidden, it clearly disproves any right to pursue vengeance or bring formal accusation.

sentences.zh: 且聖人設法，所以防淫禁暴，極言善惡，使知而避之。

translations.literal: Moreover, the sage establishes law to prevent debauchery and prohibit violence, to the utmost speak good and evil, making people know and avoid them.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the sage instituted law to restrain excess and forbid violence, defining good and evil plainly so that people might know and shun wrong.

sentences.zh: 若臨事議刑，則陷罪多矣。

translations.literal: If punishments were deliberated only when incidents arose, many would be trapped in crime.
translations.idiomatic: To decide punishments only case by case would leave countless people entangled in guilt.

sentences.zh: 惡之甚者，殺父害君，著之律令，百王罔革。

translations.literal: For the most serious evil—killing father and harming ruler—it is written in statutes; no king across the ages ever altered it.
translations.idiomatic: The worst crimes—patricide and regicide—are fixed in the code, unchanged by any king across the ages.

sentences.zh: 此制何嫌，獨求削去。

translations.literal: What objection to this regulation, alone seeking to cut it away?
translations.idiomatic: What fault is there in this rule that you alone seek its removal?

sentences.zh: 既於法無違，於事非害，宣布有年，謂不宜改。

translations.literal: Since it violates no law and harms no affair, having been promulgated for years, it is deemed unsuitable to change.
translations.idiomatic: It violates no statute, harms no interest, and has stood for years—I hold it should not be altered."

sentences.zh: 」瑗復難云：

translations.literal: " Dou Yuan again objected, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yuan rebutted:

sentences.zh: 尋局判云：「子於父母，同氣異息，終天靡報，在情一也。

translations.literal: Seeking the bureau judgment which said: "The child toward parents—same breath, different exhalations; a lifetime without repayment—in feeling, one.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing the bureau's ruling: "Toward both parents the child shares one vital breath, yet owes a debt that can never be repaid in a lifetime—in emotion they are one.

sentences.zh: 今欲論其尊卑，辨其優劣，推心未忍，訪古無據。

translations.literal: Now to discuss their honor and lowliness, distinguish superiority and inferiority—in heart one cannot bear it; inquiry of antiquity has no basis.
translations.idiomatic: Now to debate their rank and weigh one against the other—my heart cannot bear it, and antiquity offers no warrant."

sentences.zh: 」瑗以為易曰：「天尊地卑，乾坤定矣。

translations.literal: Dou Yuan thought the Changes says: "Heaven is noble, earth is low—the hexagrams Qian and Kun are fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yuan cited the Book of Changes: "Heaven is noble and earth is low—thus Qian and Kun are fixed.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「乾天也，故稱父；

translations.literal: It also says: "Qian is heaven, therefore called father;
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "Qian is heaven, and so is called father;

sentences.zh: 坤地也，故稱母。

translations.literal: Kun is earth, therefore called mother.
translations.idiomatic: Kun is earth, and so is called mother."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：乾為天，為父；

translations.literal: It also says: Qian is heaven, is father;
translations.idiomatic: It also states: Qian stands for heaven and for the father;

sentences.zh: 坤為地，為母。

translations.literal: Kun is earth, is mother.
translations.idiomatic: Kun stands for earth and for the mother.

sentences.zh: 禮喪服經曰：為父斬衰三年，為母齊衰期。

translations.literal: The Classic of Mourning Garments says: For the father, zhan mourning three years; for the mother, qi mourning one period.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Mourning Garments prescribes three years of zhan mourning for a father and one year of qi mourning for a mother.

sentences.zh: 尊卑優劣，顯在典章，何言訪古無據？

translations.literal: Honor and lowliness, superiority and inferiority—clear in canonical regulations—how say inquiry of antiquity has no basis?
translations.idiomatic: Rank and precedence are explicit in the canonical texts—how can one say antiquity offers no warrant?

sentences.zh: 局判云：「母殺其父，子復告母，母由告死，便是子殺。

translations.literal: The bureau judgment said: "The mother kills his father; the child again reports the mother—the mother dies through report, and this is the child killing.
translations.idiomatic: The bureau ruling states: "If the mother kills his father and the child then reports the mother, and the mother dies because of that report, the child has effectively killed her.

sentences.zh: 天下未有無母之國，不知此子將欲何之！

translations.literal: Under heaven there has never been a state without mothers—who knows where this child would go!
translations.idiomatic: There is no land under heaven without mothers—where would such a child turn!"

sentences.zh: 」瑗案典律，未聞母殺其父而子有隱母之義。

translations.literal: Dou Yuan examined the canonical statutes and had never heard of a principle of concealing the mother when she kills his father.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yuan searched the code and found no provision granting a son the right to conceal his mother when she kills his father.

sentences.zh: 既不告母，便是與殺父，天下豈有無父之國，此子獨得有所之乎！

translations.literal: If one does not report the mother, that is complicity in killing the father—is there under heaven a state without fathers, that this child alone would have somewhere to go!
translations.idiomatic: If the son does not report her, he is complicit in his father's murder—is there any land without fathers, that this child alone would have a place to go!

sentences.zh: 局判又云：「案春秋，莊公元年，不稱即位，文姜出故。

translations.literal: The bureau judgment also said: "Examining the Spring and Autumn Annals: in the first year of Duke Zhuang, he is not styled as ascending the throne—because Wen Jiang was driven out.
translations.idiomatic: The bureau ruling also cites: "The Spring and Autumn Annals record that in Duke Zhuang's first year he is not said to have taken the throne, because Wen Jiang had been expelled.

sentences.zh: 服虔注云：『文姜通於兄齊襄，與殺公而不反。

translations.literal: Fu Qian's commentary says: 'Wen Jiang had relations with her elder brother Duke Xiang of Qi, participated in killing the Duke and did not return.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Qian commented: 'Wen Jiang had an illicit affair with her brother Duke Xiang of Qi, took part in killing Duke Huan, and did not return home.

sentences.zh: 父殺母出，隱痛深諱，期而中練，思慕少殺，念至於母。

translations.literal: The father was killed, the mother expelled—hidden grief, deeply concealed; at the end of the first mourning period and into the second, yearning slightly diminished, thoughts reached the mother.
translations.idiomatic: Her father had been killed and her mother banished; in concealed grief he deeply hid the matter; at the midpoint of the second year of mourning, as his grief slightly eased, his thoughts turned to his mother.

sentences.zh: 故經書：三月夫人遜於齊。

translations.literal: Therefore the classic records: In the third month the lady withdrew to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the chronicle states: In the third month the lady departed for Qi.

sentences.zh: 』既有念母深諱之文，明無讎疾告列之理。

translations.literal: ' Since there is text of cherishing the mother and deeply concealing, clearly there is no principle of enmity and reporting publicly.
translations.idiomatic: Where the text shows him yearning for his mother while keeping the matter hidden, it clearly disproves any right to pursue vengeance or bring formal accusation."

sentences.zh: 」瑗尋注義，隱痛深諱者，以父為齊所殺，而母與之。

translations.literal: Dou Yuan sought the meaning of the commentary: "hidden grief, deeply concealed" means the father was killed by Qi and the mother was involved with it.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yuan examined the commentary's meaning: the phrase "hidden grief, deeply concealed" refers to the fact that his father was killed by Qi and his mother was party to it.

sentences.zh: 隱痛父死，深諱母出，故不稱即位。

translations.literal: He concealed grief over his father's death and deeply hid his mother's expulsion, therefore he is not styled as ascending the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He hid his grief over his father's death and deeply concealed his mother's banishment, and therefore is not said to have taken the throne.

sentences.zh: 非為諱母與殺也。

translations.literal: It was not for concealing the mother's participation in the killing.
translations.idiomatic: This was not a matter of concealing the mother's complicity in the murder.

sentences.zh: 是以下文以義絕，其罪不為與殺明矣。

translations.literal: Therefore in the text below, by righteousness severed, her crime is clearly not complicity in killing.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the passage below, severing ties by righteousness, makes clear that her crime was not treated as complicity in killing.

sentences.zh: [9]公羊傳曰：「君殺，子不言即位，隱之也。

translations.literal: [9] The Gongyang Commentary says: "When the ruler is killed, the son does not speak of ascending the throne—this is concealing it.
translations.idiomatic: [9] The Gongyang Commentary says: "When the ruler is killed, the son does not speak of taking the throne—this is concealment.

sentences.zh: 」期而中練，父憂少衰，始念於母，略書「夫人遜於齊」。

translations.literal: At the end of the first mourning period and into the second, grief for the father slightly diminished, he began to think of the mother, briefly recording "the lady withdrew to Qi."
translations.idiomatic: At the midpoint of the second year of mourning, as grief for his father eased somewhat, he began to think of his mother, and the chronicle briefly notes that "the lady departed for Qi."

sentences.zh: 是內諱出奔，猶為罪文。

translations.literal: This is concealing flight within, still treated as criminal wording.
translations.idiomatic: This is an internal concealment of her flight abroad, yet it is still recorded as a mark of guilt.

sentences.zh: 傳曰：「不稱姜氏，絕不為親，禮也。

translations.literal: The commentary says: "The lady is not styled Jiang—severing her as kin is ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary states: "She is not called Lady Jiang—cutting her off as kin is ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 」注云：「夫人有與殺桓之罪，絕不為親，得尊父之義。

translations.literal: The commentary says: "The lady had the crime of participating in killing Duke Huan—severing her as kin upholds the righteousness of honoring the father.
translations.idiomatic: The note explains: "The lady was guilty of complicity in Duke Huan's murder—severing her as kin upholds the principle of honoring the father.

sentences.zh: 善莊公思大義，絕有罪，故曰禮也。

translations.literal: Praising Duke Zhuang for considering great righteousness and severing the guilty, therefore it is called ritual.
translations.idiomatic: It praises Duke Zhuang for weighing great righteousness and cutting off the guilty party, and therefore calls this ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 」以大義絕有罪，得禮之衷，明有讎疾告列之理。

translations.literal: By great righteousness severing the guilty, obtaining the core of ritual—clearly there is a principle of enmity and reporting publicly.
translations.idiomatic: Severing ties with the guilty by great righteousness, in accord with the heart of ritual—this clearly supports the right to pursue vengeance and bring formal accusation.

sentences.zh: 但春秋桓、莊之際，齊為大國，通于文姜，魯公謫之。

translations.literal: But in the era of Duke Huan and Duke Zhuang of the Spring and Autumn period, Qi was a great state; Wen Jiang had relations with Duke Xiang, and Duke Huan of Lu reproached her.
translations.idiomatic: But during the reigns of Duke Huan and Duke Zhuang, Qi was a great power; Wen Jiang's affair with Duke Xiang led Duke Huan of Lu to rebuke her.

sentences.zh: 文姜以告齊襄，使公子彭生殺之。

translations.literal: Wen Jiang informed Duke Xiang of Qi, who had the prince Peng Sheng kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Jiang reported this to Duke Xiang of Qi, who had Prince Peng Sheng kill him.

sentences.zh: 魯既弱小而懼於齊。

translations.literal: Lu was weak and small and feared Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Lu was weak and small and stood in fear of Qi.

sentences.zh: 是時天子衰微，又無賢霸，故不敢讎之，又不敢告列，惟得告於齊曰：「無所歸咎，惡於諸侯，請以公子彭生除之。

translations.literal: At that time the Son of Heaven was in decline, and there was no worthy hegemon, so they dared not pursue vengeance, nor dare bring formal accusation—they could only report to Qi, saying: "There is no one else to blame; he is hated by the feudal lords—please have Prince Peng Sheng removed.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven's authority had waned, and there was no worthy hegemon, so Lu dared neither seek vengeance nor lodge a formal accusation—they could only appeal to Qi, saying: "There is no one else to blame; he is despised by the feudal lords—please have Prince Peng Sheng executed.

sentences.zh: 」齊人殺公子彭生。

translations.literal: The people of Qi killed Prince Peng Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Qi then killed Prince Peng Sheng.

sentences.zh: 案郎此斷，雖有援引，即以情推理，尚未遣惑。

translations.literal: Examining this bureau director's judgment, though it had citations, reasoning from the circumstances still did not dispel the perplexity.
translations.idiomatic: Examining this official's ruling, though it cited precedents, reasoning from the circumstances still left the issue unresolved.

sentences.zh: 事遂停寢。

translations.literal: The matter then ceased and was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was then dropped and went no further.

sentences.zh: 除大宗正卿，尋加衞將軍。

translations.literal: He was dismissed from Grand Director of the Imperial Clan, and soon after was appointed General of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was removed from the post of Grand Director of the Imperial Clan, and soon afterward was made General of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 宗室以其寒士，相與輕之。

translations.literal: The imperial clan, because he was a man of humble birth, collectively looked down on him.
translations.idiomatic: Members of the imperial clan looked down on him because he was a man of humble birth.

sentences.zh: 瑗案法推治，無所顧避，甚見讎疾。

translations.literal: Dou Yuan investigated cases according to law, without partiality or evasion, and was greatly resented.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yuan prosecuted cases by the letter of the law, without favor or evasion, and incurred much enmity.

sentences.zh: 官雖通顯，貧窘如初，清尚之操，為時所重。

translations.literal: Though his office was eminent, he remained as poor as before; his integrity and lofty conduct were highly regarded by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Though his rank was high, he remained as poor as ever; his integrity and lofty character won great respect in his time.

sentences.zh: 領本州大中正，以本官兼廷尉卿，卒官。

translations.literal: He served as Grand Assessor of his home province, and concurrently held his original office together with the post of Director of the Court of Judicial Review; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Grand Assessor of his native province while also holding the post of Director of the Court of Judicial Review; he died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈本將軍、太僕卿、濟州刺史，諡曰明。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the rank of General of the Guard, Director of the Imperial Stud, and Governor of Ji Province; his posthumous title was Ming.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as General of the Guard, Director of the Imperial Stud, and Governor of Ji Province, with the posthumous name Ming.

sentences.zh: 羊敦，字元禮，太山鉅平人，梁州刺史祉弟子也。

translations.literal: Yang Dun, courtesy name Yuanli, was a native of Juping in Mount Tai; he was a nephew of Yang Zhi, Governor of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Dun, styled Yuanli, was a native of Juping in Taishan commandery and a nephew of Yang Zhi, Governor of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 性尚閑素，學涉書史。

translations.literal: By nature he favored quiet simplicity; in learning he ranged broadly over books and histories.
translations.idiomatic: He was by nature fond of quiet simplicity and was widely versed in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 以父靈引死王事，除給事中。

translations.literal: Because his father Ling died in service to the throne, he was appointed Attendant at the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father Ling died in the performance of official duty, he was appointed Attendant at the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 出為本州別駕。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as Vice Governor of his home province.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to serve as Vice Governor of his native province.

sentences.zh: 公平正直，見有非法，敦終不判署。

translations.literal: Fair and upright, whenever he saw anything unlawful, Dun never signed or approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Just and upright, whenever he encountered anything unlawful, Dun would never sign or approve it.

sentences.zh: 後為尚書左侍郎、徐州撫軍長史。

translations.literal: Later he served as Left Assistant Director in the Ministry of State Affairs and Chief Administrator to the Military Governor of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Left Assistant Director in the Ministry of State Affairs and Chief Administrator to the Military Governor of Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 永安中，轉廷尉司直，不拜。

translations.literal: During the Yong'an era he was transferred to Directing Censor of the Court of Judicial Review, but did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yong'an period he was transferred to Directing Censor of the Court of Judicial Review, but declined the post.

sentences.zh: 拜洛陽令。

translations.literal: He was appointed Magistrate of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted appointment as Magistrate of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 後為鎮南將軍、金紫光祿大夫，遷太府少卿，轉衞將軍、廣平太守。

translations.literal: Later he served as General Who Guards the South and Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, was transferred to Vice Director of the Imperial Treasury, then became General of the Guard and Administrator of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as General Who Guards the South and as Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, was transferred to Vice Director of the Imperial Treasury, and then became General of the Guard and Administrator of Guangping commandery.

sentences.zh: 治有能名，姦吏跼蹐，秋毫無犯。

translations.literal: In governance he had a reputation for ability; corrupt officials were cramped and fearful, and not the slightest thing escaped violation.
translations.idiomatic: He gained a reputation for capable administration; corrupt officials trembled before him, and not the slightest infraction went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 雅性清儉，屬歲饑饉，家餽未至，使人外尋陂澤，採藕根而食之。

translations.literal: By nature he was pure and frugal; during a year of famine, when household provisions had not yet arrived, he sent men outside to search marshes and ponds and gathered lotus roots to eat.
translations.idiomatic: He was by nature pure and frugal; during a famine year, before household supplies arrived, he sent servants to search marshes and ponds and gathered lotus roots for food.

sentences.zh: 遇有疾苦，家人解衣質米以供之。

translations.literal: When he encountered people in distress, his family would take off their clothes and pawn them for rice to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: When he met people in hardship, his family would pawn their clothing for rice to help them.

sentences.zh: 然其為治，亦尚威嚴。

translations.literal: Yet in his governance he also valued stern authority.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in governing he also emphasized stern authority.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以其清白，賜穀一千斛、絹一百匹。

translations.literal: The court, because of his integrity, bestowed one thousand hu of grain and one hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: In recognition of his integrity, the court granted him one thousand hu of grain and one hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 興和初卒，年五十二。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xinghe he died, aged fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the start of the Xinghe era, at the age of fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 吏民奔哭，莫不悲慟。

translations.literal: Officials and common people rushed to weep; none were not deeply grieved.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners flocked to mourn him, all deeply stricken with grief.

sentences.zh: 贈都督徐兗二州諸軍事、衞大將軍、吏部尚書、兗州刺史，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: Posthumously conferred as Supervisor of All Military Affairs for the Two Provinces of Xu and Yan, Grand General of the Guard, Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and Governor of Yan Province; posthumous title Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs for Xu and Yan provinces, Grand General of the Guard, Minister of Personnel, and Governor of Yan Province, with the posthumous name Zhen.

sentences.zh: 武定初，齊獻武王以敦及中山太守蘇淑在官奉法，清約自居，宜見追褒，以厲天下，乃上言請加旌錄。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wuding, Prince Xianwu of Qi, because Dun and Zhongshan Prefect Su Shu while in office upheld the law and maintained frugal integrity, deserved posthumous commendation to encourage the realm, submitted a memorial requesting additional honors and recognition.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Wuding era, Prince Xianwu of Qi submitted a memorial requesting special honors, arguing that Yang Dun and Zhongshan Prefect Su Shu had faithfully upheld the law and lived in frugal integrity while in office, and that their example should be celebrated to inspire officials throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「昔五袴興謠，兩歧致詠，皆由仁覃千里，化洽一邦。

translations.literal: An edict said: "In former times the song of five pairs of trousers arose and the ode to double-headed grain was sung—all because benevolence spread a thousand li and civilizing influence permeated a whole realm.
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: "In former times the people sang of magistrates whose governance was so fair that even trousers were shared in twos, and the land so fertile it yielded double-headed grain—all because benevolence reached a thousand li and humane rule transformed an entire realm.

sentences.zh: 故廣平太守羊敦、故中山太守蘇淑，並器業和隱，幹用貞濟，善政聞國，清譽在民。

translations.literal: The late Guangping Prefect Yang Dun and the late Zhongshan Prefect Su Shu both had talent and character harmonious and modest, capacity and conduct upright and successful, good governance heard throughout the state, and reputations for integrity among the people.
translations.idiomatic: The late Guangping Prefect Yang Dun and the late Zhongshan Prefect Su Shu were alike in talent and modest character, upright and capable in service, their good governance known throughout the realm and their reputation for integrity cherished by the people.

sentences.zh: 方藉良才，遂登高秩，先後凋亡，朝野傷悼。

translations.literal: Just as they were relied upon for talent and had risen to lofty ranks, they perished one after another; court and countryside alike mourned.
translations.idiomatic: Just as the court had come to rely on their talents and they had risen to high office, they died in quick succession, and officials and commoners alike grieved their loss.

translations.idiomatic: Su Shu, courtesy name Zhonghe, came from Wuyi.

translations.literal: In disposition he was solid and cautious, and he had gained considerable acquaintance with the classics and their commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: He was by nature earnest and prudent, and had gained a solid grounding in the classics and their commentaries.

sentences.zh: 兄壽興，坐事為閹官。

translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Shouxing, having been condemned for an offense, was made a palace eunuch.

translations.literal: Later Shouxing became Prefect of Hejian and was granted the noble rank of Baron of Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shouxing later served as Prefect of Hejian and was enfeoffed as Baron of Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 及壽興將卒，遂冒養淑為子。

translations.literal: When Shouxing was about to die, he falsely claimed to have raised Shu as his son.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouxing was near death, he formally adopted Shu as his son, though Shu was not in fact his child.

sentences.zh: 淑，熙平中襲其爵，除司空士曹參軍。

translations.literal: Shu, in the Xiping era, inherited his rank and was appointed Army Staff Officer of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiping era, Shu inherited Shouxing's noble rank and was appointed staff officer in the Bureau of Works.

sentences.zh: 尋轉太學博士、厲威將軍、員外散騎侍郎。

translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Erudite of the Imperial Academy, given the rank of General Who Inspires Awe, and appointed Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier.

translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Commandant of the Convoy and concurrently served as Palace Attendant Censor.

translations.idiomatic: While on a mission to Jizhou, he encountered Gao Ganqiu, who had seized Provincial Governor Yuan Yan and rebelled from the city; Shu gave his support to the cause.

translations.idiomatic: Gao Ganqiu appointed Shu acting administrator of Wuyi commandery.

translations.idiomatic: Before long Erzhu Rugui marched on the commandery with troops, and Shu fled back to the capital.

translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Left General and Grand Master of Palace Counsel, and served as acting magistrate of Heyin.

translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Administrator of Leling and sent out to take up the post.

translations.literal: Shu in the commandery pacified and comforted the people, and had a great reputation among them.
translations.idiomatic: In the commandery, Shu governed with a gentle hand and won a fine reputation among the people.

translations.idiomatic: After less than two years in office, he submitted his resignation on grounds of illness, and the emperor approved it—but vast numbers of officials and commoners, young and old alike, petitioned begging that he be kept on.

sentences.zh: 後歷滎陽太守，亦有能名。

translations.literal: Later he served as Prefect of Xingyang, and also had a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Prefect of Xingyang, where he likewise earned a reputation for capable administration.

sentences.zh: 加中軍將軍、司徒從事中郎。

translations.literal: He was additionally given the titles General of the Central Army and Attendant Gentleman of the Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to General of the Central Army and Attendant Gentleman on the staff of the Minister over the Masses.

translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xinghe, he was appointed Prefect of Zhongshan.

translations.idiomatic: In the third year he died in office.

translations.literal: His son Qiji served as the king's attendant and reported upward: According to examination, the event is found in Zuozhuan, Duke Xiang, year 22; this is not quoting the original text, but "reported upward" makes no sense—it is suspected that "shang" is a corruption of "wang", referring to King Kang of Chu informing Qiji of his wish to kill Zinan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qiji served as the king's attendant and reported upward: The incident appears in Zuozhuan, Duke Xiang, year 22; this is not a direct quotation, but "reported upward" (shanggao) is meaningless—it is suspected that shang is a corruption of wang, referring to King Kang of Chu informing Qiji of his intent to kill Zinan.

sentences.zh: 其罪不為與殺明矣 按竇瑗認為服虔注「隱痛深諱」，乃是諱母出，「非為諱母與殺也」。

translations.literal: That the crime was not complicity in murder is clear: According to examination, Dou Yuan held that Fu Qian's gloss "deeply concealing grief out of taboo" refers to concealing the mother's disgrace—"not concealing complicity in the mother's murder".
translations.idiomatic: That the crime was not complicity in murder is clear: On examination, Dou Yuan understood Fu Qian's gloss "deeply concealing grief out of taboo" as concealing the mother's disgrace—"not concealing the mother's complicity in murder".

sentences.zh: 若作「其罪不為與殺」，則是說文姜本無參與殺桓公之罪，和他辯論的本題不合，且與下文引服注「夫人有與殺桓之罪」語相背。

translations.literal: If read as "the crime was not complicity in murder," that would mean Wen Jiang had no part in Duke Huan's murder, which does not accord with the main point of his argument, and contradicts below the citation of Fu Qian's gloss "the lady had a part in murdering Huan".
translations.idiomatic: If rendered as "the crime was not complicity in murder," it would mean Wen Jiang bore no part in Duke Huan's murder—which misses the point of Dou Yuan's argument and contradicts the Fu Qian gloss quoted below, "the lady had a part in murdering Huan".

sentences.zh: 這裏「罪」當是「諱」字之訛，言「其諱不為與殺」，和上下文相貫。

translations.literal: Here "zui" must be a corruption of "hui"; the meaning is "the concealment was not complicity in murder," which coheres with the surrounding context.
translations.idiomatic: Here zui (crime) should be read as a corruption of hui (concealment, taboo), yielding "the concealment was not complicity in murder"—which fits the surrounding context.
